1	/**
2	 * Main Cloudflare Worker entry point for the Paperclip API.
3	 *
4	 * This file:
5	 *   1. Creates a Hono app and mounts route definitions extracted from the
6	 *      server's Express routers via the express-router-bridge.
7	 *   2. Implements the first-run setup gate (redirects to /setup until KV flag is set).
8	 *   3. Handles Cloudflare Queues message batches (plugin job fanout, heartbeat dispatch).
9	 *   4. Handles Cloudflare Cron Triggers (heartbeat sweep, budget checks, DB backup).
10	 *   5. Re-exports all Durable Object and Workflow classes so Wrangler can
11	 *      register them -- they must be named exports from the Worker's main module.
12	 *
13	 * Routes skipped (use Node-only features -- left as 501 TODOs):
14	 *   - adapterRoutes       -- reads packages from disk
15	 *   - pluginRoutes        -- SSE, child processes, scoped plugin API
16	 *   - pluginUiStaticRoutes -- fs.readFileSync / res.sendFile
17	 *   - companySkillRoutes  -- local filesystem (CF version: cf-company-skills.ts)
18	 *   - accessRoutes        -- reads bundled SKILL.md files from disk
19	 *   - instanceDatabaseBackupRoutes -- pg_dump
20	 *
21	 * Architecture note on per-request DB injection:
22	 *   Route handlers (Handler functions) capture a `db` and `storage` reference
23	 *   from the service factories at the time the Express Router is built. Because
24	 *   the real `db` comes from Hyperdrive (a per-request binding), we rebuild the
25	 *   Express Routers on the FIRST request of each cold start and cache the
26	 *   extracted route definitions for subsequent requests in the same isolate.
27	 *
28	 *   Hono routes are registered at module load time as thin proxies that
29	 *   forward to the lazily-built route definitions.
30	 */

111	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
112	// Per-isolate route cache
113	//
114	// Workers isolates are long-lived within a datacenter edge node. We build the
115	// Express Routers (and extract RouteDefinitions) once per isolate, keyed on
116	// the Hyperdrive connection string (proxy for "same DB config").
117	//
118	// Subsequent requests in the same isolate reuse the cached routes, skipping
119	// the router construction overhead.
120	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
121	
122	interface CompiledRoute {
123	  route: RouteDefinition;
124	  re: RegExp;
125	  paramNames: string[];
126	}
127	
128	interface RouteCache {
129	  routes: RouteDefinition[];
130	  compiled: CompiledRoute[];
131	  db: Db;
132	  storage: StorageService;
133	  hyperdriveConnStr: string;
134	}

136	let routeCache: RouteCache | null = null;
137	
138	// Convert an Express-style path pattern (with :param segments) to a RegExp.
139	function pathToRegex(path: string): { re: RegExp; paramNames: string[] } {
140	  const paramNames: string[] = [];
141	  const pattern = path
142	    .replace(/[$()*+.?[\\\]^{|}]/g, "\\$&")
143	    .replace(/:([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)/g, (_match, name: string) => {
144	      paramNames.push(name);
145	      return "([^/]+)";
146	    });
147	  return { re: new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`), paramNames };
148	}
149	
150	function buildRouteCache(env: Env): RouteCache {
151	  const db = createHyperdriveDb(env.HYPERDRIVE);
152	  const r2Provider = new R2Provider(env.PAPERCLIP_STORAGE, {
153	    bucket: env.STORAGE_R2_BUCKET ?? "paperclip-storage",
154	    prefix: env.STORAGE_R2_PREFIX ?? "",
155	  });
156	  const storage = createCfStorageService(r2Provider) as unknown as StorageService;
157	
158	  function ext(router: unknown, prefix: string): RouteDefinition[] {
159	    return extractRoutesFromRouter(router, prefix);
160	  }
161	
162	  const routes: RouteDefinition[] = [
163	    ...ext(companyRoutes(db, storage), "/api/companies"),
164	    ...ext(agentRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
165	    ...ext(assetRoutes(db, storage), "/api"),
166	    ...ext(projectRoutes(db), "/api"),
167	    ...ext(issueRoutes(db, storage, {}), "/api"),
168	    ...ext(issueTreeControlRoutes(db), "/api"),
169	    ...ext(routineRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
170	    ...ext(environmentRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
171	    ...ext(executionWorkspaceRoutes(db), "/api"),
172	    ...ext(goalRoutes(db), "/api"),
173	    ...ext(approvalRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
174	    ...ext(secretRoutes(db), "/api"),
175	    ...ext(costRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
176	    ...ext(activityRoutes(db), "/api"),
177	    ...ext(dashboardRoutes(db), "/api"),
178	    ...ext(userProfileRoutes(db), "/api"),
179	    ...ext(sidebarBadgeRoutes(db), "/api"),
180	    ...ext(sidebarPreferenceRoutes(db), "/api"),
181	    ...ext(inboxDismissalRoutes(db), "/api"),
182	    ...ext(instanceSettingsRoutes(db), "/api"),
183	    ...ext(llmRoutes(db), "/api"),
184	    ...ext(authRoutes(db), "/api"),
185	  ];
186	
187	  const compiled: CompiledRoute[] = routes.map((route) => ({
188	    route,
189	    ...pathToRegex(route.path),
190	  }));
191	
192	  return { routes, compiled, db, storage, hyperdriveConnStr: env.HYPERDRIVE.connectionString };
193	}
194	
195	function getRouteCache(env: Env): RouteCache {
196	  if (!routeCache || routeCache.hyperdriveConnStr !== env.HYPERDRIVE.connectionString) {
197	    routeCache = buildRouteCache(env);
198	    console.log(`[CF Worker] Built route cache: ${routeCache.routes.length} routes`);
199	  }
200	  return routeCache;
201	}

14	 * declare a local structural equivalent so this file compiles without
15	 * requiring the workers-types package at import time.
16	 */
17	export interface HyperdriveBinding {
18	  /** The connection string Cloudflare injects — points to the Hyperdrive proxy. */
19	  connectionString: string;
20	}

22	/**
23	 * Creates a Drizzle `Db` instance backed by Cloudflare Hyperdrive.
24	 *
25	 * Hyperdrive terminates the Postgres connection pool near the Worker and
26	 * forwards queries to the upstream Neon/Postgres database over a long-lived
27	 * TCP connection. The `postgres-js` driver is compatible with the Workers
28	 * `nodejs_compat` flag, which provides a polyfilled TCP socket layer.
29	 *
30	 * Pool size is capped at 5 — each Worker invocation is short-lived so a
31	 * large pool wastes Hyperdrive connection slots.
32	 *
33	 * @param hyperdrive - The Hyperdrive binding from the Worker `Env`.
34	 */
35	export function createHyperdriveDb(hyperdrive: HyperdriveBinding): Db {
36	  // max: 5 keeps connection usage low across concurrent invocations.
37	  // prepare: false disables prepared-statement caching because Hyperdrive
38	  // routes across multiple upstream connections and cannot share PS state.
39	  const sql = postgres(hyperdrive.connectionString, {
40	    max: 5,
41	    prepare: false,
42	  });
43	  // drizzle-orm's postgres-js adapter returns a type that is structurally
44	  // identical to the `Db` exported from @paperclipai/db. The cast via
45	  // `unknown` is necessary only because the generic parameters differ at
46	  // the type level; the runtime shapes are identical.
47	  return drizzle(sql, { schema }) as unknown as Db;
48	}

```mjs
/**
 * Custom esbuild bundler for the Cloudflare Worker.
 *
 * Wrangler's built-in esbuild cannot mark specific packages as external, so we
 * pre-bundle the worker here and point wrangler to the output with --no-bundle.
 *
 * Packages marked external:
 *   - embedded-postgres / @embedded-postgres/*  — native Node binaries, never
 *     called in CF (Hyperdrive handles DB).
 *   - jsdom                                      — used only for SVG sanitization
 *     in assets.ts; not available in Workers runtime.
 *   - node:sqlite                                — Node 22.5+ built-in pulled in
 *     by undici@7 (via jsdom); unavailable in Workers.
 */

import { build } from "esbuild";
import { fileURLToPath } from "url";
import path from "path";

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));

await build({
  entryPoints: [path.join(__dirname, "src/worker/api.ts")],
  bundle: true,
  outfile: path.join(__dirname, "dist/worker.js"),
  format: "esm",
  target: "es2022",
  platform: "browser",
  conditions: ["worker", "browser", "module"],
  mainFields: ["module", "main"],
  external: [
    // Node-only embedded postgres binaries
    "embedded-postgres",
    "@embedded-postgres/*",
    // SVG sanitization (not available in Workers; dynamic import in assets.ts will throw at runtime for SVG uploads)
    "jsdom",
    // Node 22.5+ built-in pulled in transitively via jsdom → undici@7
    "node:sqlite",
  ],
  // Keep dynamic imports as-is so wrangler/miniflare can handle code splitting
  splitting: false,
  define: {
    "process.env.NODE_ENV": '"production"',
  },
  logLevel: "info",
});

console.log("Worker bundle written to dist/worker.js");

```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-04-30 17:11:32Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```mjs
/**
 * Custom esbuild bundler for the Cloudflare Worker.
 *
 * Wrangler's built-in esbuild cannot mark specific packages as external, so we
 * pre-bundle the worker here and point wrangler to the output with --no-bundle.
 *
 * Approach:
 *   - platform: "neutral" so esbuild doesn't inject browser/node polyfills
 *   - node:* builtins are external — provided at runtime by CF nodejs_compat
 *   - cloudflare:* modules are external — provided by the CF runtime
 *   - embedded-postgres / @embedded-postgres/* — native Node binaries, not available
 *     in Workers; no CF code path reaches these
 *   - jsdom — Node-only; SVG sanitization path (assets.ts) will throw at runtime in CF
 *   - node:sqlite — pulled in by undici@7 via jsdom; not available in Workers
 */

import { build } from "esbuild";
import { fileURLToPath } from "url";
import path from "path";

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));

// Node.js built-ins that CF provides via nodejs_compat flag
const NODE_BUILTINS = [
  "node:assert", "node:async_hooks", "node:buffer", "node:child_process",
  "node:cluster", "node:console", "node:constants", "node:crypto",
  "node:dgram", "node:diagnostics_channel", "node:dns", "node:domain",
  "node:events", "node:fs", "node:fs/promises", "node:http", "node:http2",
  "node:https", "node:inspector", "node:module", "node:net", "node:os",
  "node:path", "node:perf_hooks", "node:process", "node:querystring",
  "node:readline", "node:repl", "node:stream", "node:stream/consumers",
  "node:stream/promises", "node:stream/web", "node:string_decoder",
  "node:sys", "node:timers", "node:timers/promises", "node:tls",
  "node:trace_events", "node:tty", "node:url", "node:util", "node:util/types",
  "node:v8", "node:vm", "node:wasi", "node:worker_threads", "node:zlib",
  // Without "node:" prefix (legacy imports)
  "assert", "async_hooks", "buffer", "child_process", "cluster", "console",
  "constants", "crypto", "dgram", "diagnostics_channel", "dns", "domain",
  "events", "fs", "http", "http2", "https", "inspector", "module", "net",
  "os", "path", "perf_hooks", "process", "querystring", "readline", "repl",
  "stream", "string_decoder", "sys", "timers", "tls", "trace_events", "tty",
  "url", "util", "v8", "vm", "wasi", "worker_threads", "zlib",
  // Node 22.5+ built-in pulled in by undici@7 — not available in Workers
  "node:sqlite",
];

await build({
  entryPoints: [path.join(__dirname, "src/worker/api.ts")],
  bundle: true,
  outfile: path.join(__dirname, "dist/worker.js"),
  format: "esm",
  target: "es2022",
  platform: "neutral",
  conditions: ["workerd", "worker", "browser", "module"],
  mainFields: ["module", "main"],
  external: [
    // CF runtime modules
    "cloudflare:*",
    // Node built-ins (provided by nodejs_compat)
    ...NODE_BUILTINS,
    // Node-only packages not available in CF Workers
    "embedded-postgres",
    "@embedded-postgres/*",
    "jsdom",
  ],
  splitting: false,
  define: {
    "process.env.NODE_ENV": '"production"',
  },
  logLevel: "info",
});

console.log("Worker bundle written to dist/worker.js");

```

50	 *

52	 * root-mounted catch-all).
53	 */
54	function extractPathFromLayerRegexp(layer: RouterLayer): string {
55	  if (!layer.regexp) return "";
56	  const src = layer.regexp.source;
57	  // Pattern produced by Express for a simple path prefix like "/companies":
58	  //   ^\\/companies\\/?(?=\\/|$)

26	 *   `Handler` so Cloudflare Workers can extract it via the express-router-bridge.

49	          companyIds: (expressActor as { companyIds?: string[] }).companyIds,

51	          keyId: (expressActor as { keyId?: string }).keyId,

```typescript
/**
 * cf-express-shim.ts
 *
 * Zero-dependency replacement for `express` used in the Cloudflare Worker build.
 *
 * The server route factories call `Router()` and register routes with
 * router.get/post/patch/delete/put/use(). The Cloudflare adapter then walks
 * router.stack via express-router-bridge to extract the transport-agnostic
 * Handler functions (tagged with __handler by expressHandler).
 *
 * This shim replicates only the Express Router stack format that
 * express-router-bridge.ts expects:
 *   - Concrete routes: layer.route = { path, methods, stack: [{ handle }] }
 *   - Nested routers: layer.name = "router", layer.handle = nestedRouter,
 *                     layer.regexp = (Express-style prefix regexp)
 *
 * No Node.js built-ins are used — safe for the CF Workers runtime.
 */

type MiddlewareFn = ((...args: unknown[]) => unknown) & { __handler?: unknown };

interface RouteLayer {
  route: {
    path: string;
    methods: Record<string, boolean>;
    stack: Array<{ handle: MiddlewareFn }>;
  };
}

interface RouterMountLayer {
  name: "router";
  handle: CfRouter;
  regexp: RegExp;
  keys: unknown[];
}

type StackLayer = RouteLayer | RouterMountLayer;

export interface CfRouter {
  stack: StackLayer[];
  get(path: string, ...fns: MiddlewareFn[]): this;
  post(path: string, ...fns: MiddlewareFn[]): this;
  patch(path: string, ...fns: MiddlewareFn[]): this;
  put(path: string, ...fns: MiddlewareFn[]): this;
  delete(path: string, ...fns: MiddlewareFn[]): this;
  use(prefix: string | CfRouter, ...rest: CfRouter[]): this;
}

function buildRouteLayer(method: string, path: string, fns: MiddlewareFn[]): RouteLayer {
  return {
    route: {
      path,
      methods: { [method]: true },
      stack: fns.map((handle) => ({ handle })),
    },
  };
}

function prefixToRegexp(prefix: string): RegExp {
  // Mirror the regexp format Express produces for app.use('/prefix', router):
  //   /^\\/prefix\/?(?=\/|$)/i
  // express-router-bridge.ts reverses this via extractPathFromLayerRegexp.
  const escaped = prefix.replace(/\//g, "\\/");
  return new RegExp(`^\${escaped}\\/?(?=\\/|$)`, "i");
}

function createRouter(): CfRouter {
  const router: CfRouter = {
    stack: [],
    get(path, ...fns) { this.stack.push(buildRouteLayer("get", path, fns)); return this; },
    post(path, ...fns) { this.stack.push(buildRouteLayer("post", path, fns)); return this; },
    patch(path, ...fns) { this.stack.push(buildRouteLayer("patch", path, fns)); return this; },
    put(path, ...fns) { this.stack.push(buildRouteLayer("put", path, fns)); return this; },
    delete(path, ...fns) { this.stack.push(buildRouteLayer("delete", path, fns)); return this; },
    use(prefix, ...rest) {
      if (typeof prefix === "string") {
        for (const nested of rest) {
          router.stack.push({
            name: "router",
            handle: nested,
            regexp: prefixToRegexp(prefix),
            keys: [],
          });
        }
      } else {
        // router.use(nestedRouter) — no prefix
        router.stack.push({
          name: "router",
          handle: prefix,
          regexp: prefixToRegexp(""),
          keys: [],
        });
      }
      return this;
    },
  };
  return router;
}

// Default export matches express's export shape as used in the route files:
//   import { Router } from "express"
export const Router = createRouter;

// Type-only re-exports so TypeScript is satisfied when route files do
//   import type { Request, Response, NextFunction } from "express"
// (type-only imports are erased at compile time, so no stubs needed)
export type Request = Record<string, unknown>;
export type Response = Record<string, unknown>;
export type NextFunction = () => void;
export type RequestHandler = MiddlewareFn;

```

/**
 * Custom esbuild bundler for the Cloudflare Worker.
 *
 * Wrangler's built-in esbuild cannot mark specific packages as external or
 * alias individual modules, so we pre-bundle the worker here and point wrangler
 * to the output with --no-bundle.
 *
 * Two categories of problematic packages:
 *
 * 1. Available in CF Workers via nodejs_compat → mark as `external` so the CF
 *    runtime resolves them (node:crypto, node:stream, node:path, etc.)
 *
 * 2. NOT available in CF Workers (node:http, node:net, node:tls, node:fs, etc.)
 *    → alias to lightweight stubs bundled into the output. If the CF runtime tried
 *    to resolve these as externals it would crash on startup.
 *
 * Other stubs:
 *   - express → cf-express-shim (zero-dep Router that Express-router-bridge can walk)
 *   - embedded-postgres / @embedded-postgres/* → external (never called in CF)
 *   - jsdom → external (SVG sanitize path throws at runtime; acceptable for CF)
 */

import { build } from "esbuild";
import { fileURLToPath } from "url";
import path from "path";

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const SHIMS = path.join(__dirname, "src/shims");

// Node.js built-ins CF Workers DOES provide via nodejs_compat.
// Mark external → CF runtime resolves them at runtime.
const CF_PROVIDED_BUILTINS = [
  "node:assert", "node:async_hooks", "node:buffer", "node:crypto",
  "node:diagnostics_channel", "node:events", "node:module",
  "node:path", "node:perf_hooks", "node:process", "node:querystring",
  "node:stream", "node:stream/consumers", "node:stream/promises",
  "node:stream/web", "node:string_decoder", "node:timers",
  "node:timers/promises", "node:url", "node:util", "node:util/types",
  "node:worker_threads", "node:zlib",
  // Without "node:" prefix (legacy imports resolved by CF runtime too)
  "assert", "async_hooks", "buffer", "crypto", "diagnostics_channel",
  "events", "module", "path", "perf_hooks", "process", "querystring",
  "stream", "string_decoder", "timers", "url", "util", "zlib",
  // node:sqlite (Node 22.5+) — only referenced in try/catch inside undici@7;
  // the CF runtime will reject it but that code path is never reached.
  "node:sqlite",
  // Node-only packages not available in CF — never called in CF code paths
  "embedded-postgres",
  "@embedded-postgres/*",
  "jsdom",
];

await build({
  entryPoints: [path.join(__dirname, "src/worker/api.ts")],
  bundle: true,
  outfile: path.join(__dirname, "dist/worker.js"),
  format: "esm",
  target: "es2022",
  platform: "neutral",
  conditions: ["workerd", "worker", "browser", "module"],
  mainFields: ["module", "main"],
  external: [
    "cloudflare:*",
    ...CF_PROVIDED_BUILTINS,
  ],
  alias: {
    // Express replacement: zero-dep CF-safe Router shim
    "express": path.join(__dirname, "src/http/cf-express-shim.ts"),

    // Node.js APIs NOT available in CF Workers — stub them so the bundle
    // doesn't fail to load (code that calls these throws at runtime, which
    // is acceptable since these paths are not exercised in CF).
    "node:http":          path.join(SHIMS, "node-http.ts"),
    "http":               path.join(SHIMS, "node-http.ts"),
    "node:https":         path.join(SHIMS, "node-https.ts"),
    "https":              path.join(SHIMS, "node-https.ts"),
    "node:net":           path.join(SHIMS, "node-net.ts"),
    "net":                path.join(SHIMS, "node-net.ts"),
    "node:tls":           path.join(SHIMS, "node-tls.ts"),
    "tls":                path.join(SHIMS, "node-tls.ts"),
    "node:fs":            path.join(SHIMS, "node-fs.ts"),
    "fs":                 path.join(SHIMS, "node-fs.ts"),
    "node:fs/promises":   path.join(SHIMS, "node-fs.ts"),
    "node:child_process": path.join(SHIMS, "node-child-process.ts"),
    "child_process":      path.join(SHIMS, "node-child-process.ts"),
    "node:os":            path.join(SHIMS, "node-os.ts"),
    "os":                 path.join(SHIMS, "node-os.ts"),
  },
  splitting: false,
  define: {
    "process.env.NODE_ENV": '"production"',
  },
  logLevel: "info",
});

console.log("Worker bundle written to dist/worker.js");

```

// Shim for the "process" module — provides named exports that some packages
// destructure from it (e.g. `import { versions, env } from "process"`).
// CF Workers expose process as a global but its module doesn't have all named exports.

// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
const _proc: any = (typeof process !== "undefined") ? process : {};

export const versions: Record<string, string> = _proc.versions ?? { node: "18.0.0" };
export const env: Record<string, string | undefined> = _proc.env ?? {};
export const platform: string = _proc.platform ?? "linux";
export const arch: string = _proc.arch ?? "x64";
export const version: string = _proc.version ?? "v18.0.0";
export const argv: string[] = _proc.argv ?? [];
export const cwd = () => _proc.cwd?.() ?? "/";
export const exit = (code?: number) => _proc.exit?.(code);
export const hrtime = _proc.hrtime ?? (() => [0, 0]);
export const nextTick = (fn: () => void) => _proc.nextTick ? _proc.nextTick(fn) : Promise.resolve().then(fn);
export const pid: number = _proc.pid ?? 1;

// Re-export the process object as default
export default _proc;

```

```typescript
/**
 * CF Workers-compatible pino shim.
 *
 * The real pino requires Node.js APIs (events, worker_threads, etc.) that are
 * not available in the Workers runtime. This shim provides the same interface
 * backed by console.log/warn/error so server code works without changes.
 */

type LogLevel = "trace" | "debug" | "info" | "warn" | "error" | "fatal";
type LogFn = (msg: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;

const LEVELS: Record<LogLevel, number> = {
  trace: 10, debug: 20, info: 30, warn: 40, error: 50, fatal: 60,
};

function makeLogger(bindings: Record<string, unknown> = {}, minLevel: LogLevel = "info"): PinoLogger {
  const minNum = LEVELS[minLevel] ?? 30;

  function logAt(level: LogLevel, ...args: unknown[]) {
    if ((LEVELS[level] ?? 0) < minNum) return;
    const [msgOrObj, ...rest] = args;
    const context = { ...bindings };
    let msg: string;
    if (typeof msgOrObj === "string") {
      msg = msgOrObj;
    } else if (msgOrObj && typeof msgOrObj === "object") {
      Object.assign(context, msgOrObj);
      msg = (rest[0] as string) ?? "";
    } else {
      msg = String(msgOrObj ?? "");
    }
    const entry = JSON.stringify({ level: LEVELS[level], msg, ...context });
    if (level === "error" || level === "fatal") console.error(entry);
    else if (level === "warn") console.warn(entry);
    else console.log(entry);
  }

  const logger: PinoLogger = {
    level: minLevel,
    trace: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("trace", ...args),
    debug: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("debug", ...args),
    info: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("info", ...args),
    warn: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("warn", ...args),
    error: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("error", ...args),
    fatal: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("fatal", ...args),
    child: (childBindings: Record<string, unknown>) =>
      makeLogger({ ...bindings, ...childBindings }, minLevel),
    isLevelEnabled: (level: string) => (LEVELS[level as LogLevel] ?? 0) >= minNum,
    // pino compat properties
    bindings: () => ({ ...bindings }),
    flush: () => {},
    setBindings: (_: Record<string, unknown>) => {},
    // pino v9 adds these
    silent: () => {},
  };
  return logger;
}

interface PinoLogger {
  level: string;
  trace: LogFn;
  debug: LogFn;
  info: LogFn;
  warn: LogFn;
  error: LogFn;
  fatal: LogFn;
  child: (bindings: Record<string, unknown>) => PinoLogger;
  isLevelEnabled: (level: string) => boolean;
  bindings: () => Record<string, unknown>;
  flush: () => void;
  setBindings: (bindings: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
  silent: () => void;
}

// pino(opts?) or pino(opts?, stream?)
function pino(opts?: Record<string, unknown> | null): PinoLogger {
  const level = (opts?.level as LogLevel) ?? "info";
  return makeLogger({}, level);
}

// pino.destination() stub
pino.destination = () => ({ write: () => {} });
// pino.transport() stub
pino.transport = () => ({ write: () => {} });
// pino.levels compat
pino.levels = { values: LEVELS };
// pino.stdSerializers
pino.stdSerializers = {
  err: (e: Error) => ({ type: e.name, msg: e.message, stack: e.stack }),
  req: (r: unknown) => r,
  res: (r: unknown) => r,
};

export default pino;
export { pino };

```

/**
 * CF Workers replacement for server/src/middleware/logger.ts
 *
 * The Node.js logger writes to a local file using pino-pretty + pino transports.
 * In CF Workers, file I/O is unavailable. This shim replaces it with a
 * console-backed logger that has the same export shape.
 */

import pino from "./pino-shim.js";

export const logger = pino({ level: "info" });

// httpLogger is an Express middleware — never used in CF (we use Hono directly).
// Export a no-op so any import of httpLogger doesn't crash at module load.
export const httpLogger = (_req: unknown, _res: unknown, next: () => void) => next?.();

// CF Workers replacement for multer.
// File uploads in CF Workers use Request.formData() instead of multer middleware.
// This shim provides the same API shape so the module loads without error;
// the actual upload routes will throw at request time if invoked.

class MulterError extends Error {
  code: string;
  field?: string;
  constructor(code: string, field?: string) {
    super(code);
    this.name = "MulterError";
    this.code = code;
    this.field = field;
  }
}

const noopMiddleware = (_req: unknown, _res: unknown, next: (err?: unknown) => void) => next();

function multer(_opts?: unknown) {
  const middleware = {
    single: (_field?: string) => noopMiddleware,
    array: (_field?: string, _maxCount?: number) => noopMiddleware,
    fields: (_fields?: unknown) => noopMiddleware,
    none: () => noopMiddleware,
    any: () => noopMiddleware,
  };
  return middleware;
}

multer.memoryStorage = () => ({});
multer.diskStorage = (_opts?: unknown) => ({});
multer.MulterError = MulterError;

export default multer;
export { MulterError };

```

/**
 * express-router-bridge.ts
 *
 * Walks an Express Router's internal `.stack` to extract route definitions that
 * carry a `__handler` tag (set by the tagged `expressHandler` wrapper in
 * `server/src/http/express-adapter.ts`). The extracted definitions are the
 * transport-agnostic `Handler` functions that can be mounted directly on the
 * Hono app without pulling in any Node-specific Express machinery.
 *
 * This file is Workers-safe: it imports only type-level dependencies from the
 * server package and performs no Node-only I/O at runtime. The Express Router
 * object is passed in as an opaque `unknown` and interrogated structurally.
 */

import type { Handler, RouteDefinition } from "../../../../server/src/http/types.js";

/** A function that may carry the `__handler` tag set by `expressHandler`. */
type TaggedFn = ((...args: unknown[]) => unknown) & { __handler?: Handler };

/**
 * Shape of a single layer inside an Express Router's internal `.stack` array.
 * These are not publicly typed by Express, so we define a local structural
 * interface that matches what Express 4.x and 5.x actually produce at runtime.
 */
interface RouterLayer {
  /** Present when this layer is a concrete route (app.get / app.post / etc.). */
  route?: {
    path: string;
    methods: Record<string, boolean>;
    stack: Array<{ handle: TaggedFn }>;
  };
  /** "router" when this layer wraps a nested Router (app.use('/prefix', router)). */
  name?: string;
  /** The nested Router object when name === "router". */
  handle?: { stack?: RouterLayer[] };
  /** The compiled regexp Express stores for the mount prefix. */
  regexp?: RegExp;
  /** Named capture groups extracted from the regexp. */
  keys?: Array<{ name: string }>;
}

/**
 * Reverse-engineers the mount prefix Express stored as a regexp back into a
 * plain path string.
 *
 * Express generates regexps like:
 *   `/^\/companies\/?(?=\/|$)/i`
 * from a prefix like `/companies`. We extract the literal path segment from
 * the known pattern so we can rebuild full route paths for nested routers.
 *
 * Returns an empty string when the layer has no extractable prefix (e.g. the
 * root-mounted catch-all).
 */
function extractPathFromLayerRegexp(layer: RouterLayer): string {
  if (!layer.regexp) return "";
  const src = layer.regexp.source;
  // Pattern produced by Express for a simple path prefix like "/companies":
  //   ^\\/companies\\/?(?=\\/|$)
  const m = src.match(/^\^\\\/(.+?)\\\/\?\(\?=\\\/\|\$\)/);
  if (m) return "/" + m[1].replace(/\\\//g, "/");
  return "";
}

/**
 * Recursively walks an Express Router's `.stack` and returns all
 * `RouteDefinition` objects whose innermost handler carries a `__handler` tag.
 *
 * @param routerObj - The Express `Router` instance (typed as `unknown` to avoid
 *   importing Express at the call site, which would pull in Node-only types).
 * @param prefix - The path prefix accumulated from outer `app.use()` calls.
 */
export function extractRoutesFromRouter(
  routerObj: unknown,
  prefix = "",
): RouteDefinition[] {
  const router = routerObj as { stack?: RouterLayer[] };
  const defs: RouteDefinition[] = [];

  for (const layer of router.stack ?? []) {
    if (layer.route) {
      // This layer is a concrete route (GET /foo, POST /bar, etc.)
      const path = prefix + layer.route.path;
      for (const [method, enabled] of Object.entries(layer.route.methods)) {
        if (!enabled) continue;
        for (const rl of layer.route.stack) {
          if (rl.handle.__handler) {
            defs.push({
              method: method.toUpperCase() as RouteDefinition["method"],
              path,
              handler: rl.handle.__handler,
            });
            break; // Only take the first tagged handler per method
          }
        }

import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/postgres-js";
import postgres from "postgres";
// Import the schema directly from the workspace source. The package.json exports
// map "./*" to "./src/*.ts", so "@paperclipai/db/schema" resolves to
// packages/db/src/schema.ts — but that file does not exist; the entry is
// packages/db/src/schema/index.ts. We use a relative path to be explicit and
// avoid relying on bundler heuristics for directory index resolution.
import * as schema from "../../../db/src/schema/index.js";
import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";

/**
 * Minimal interface that matches the Cloudflare Hyperdrive binding shape.
 * The full type is `Hyperdrive` from `@cloudflare/workers-types`, but we
 * declare a local structural equivalent so this file compiles without
 * requiring the workers-types package at import time.
 */
export interface HyperdriveBinding {
  /** The connection string Cloudflare injects — points to the Hyperdrive proxy. */
  connectionString: string;
}

/**
 * Creates a Drizzle `Db` instance backed by Cloudflare Hyperdrive.
 *
 * Hyperdrive terminates the Postgres connection pool near the Worker and
 * forwards queries to the upstream Neon/Postgres database over a long-lived
 * TCP connection. The `postgres-js` driver is compatible with the Workers
 * `nodejs_compat` flag, which provides a polyfilled TCP socket layer.
 *
 * Pool size is capped at 5 — each Worker invocation is short-lived so a
 * large pool wastes Hyperdrive connection slots.
 *
 * @param hyperdrive - The Hyperdrive binding from the Worker `Env`.
 */
export function createHyperdriveDb(hyperdrive: HyperdriveBinding): Db {
  // max: 5 keeps connection usage low across concurrent invocations.
  // prepare: false disables prepared-statement caching because Hyperdrive
  // routes across multiple upstream connections and cannot share PS state.
  const sql = postgres(hyperdrive.connectionString, {
    max: 5,
    prepare: false,
  });
  // drizzle-orm's postgres-js adapter returns a type that is structurally
  // identical to the `Db` exported from @paperclipai/db. The cast via
  // `unknown` is necessary only because the generic parameters differ at
  // the type level; the runtime shapes are identical.
  return drizzle(sql, { schema }) as unknown as Db;
}

So if I call `companyRoutes` with a fresh db on each request, I automatically get fresh closures that close over the new db. The fix is straightforward: make `getCompiledRoutes` stop caching and just create fresh routes every time.

Writing the function... I'm realizing the performance hit is minimal—building 229 routes is just object creation at 1-5ms, and the Postgres client creation is fast since connections happen lazily on first query. So I can safely rebuild routes fresh per request without caching, but I should consider caching just the compiled route paths and regexes since those are truly static, while keeping the handlers fresh so they close over new database instances.

String: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Per-isolate route cache
//
// Workers isolates are long-lived within a datacenter edge node. We build the
// Express Routers (and extract RouteDefinitions) once per isolate, keyed on
// the Hyperdrive connection string (proxy for "same DB config").
//
// Subsequent requests in the same isolate reuse the cached routes, skipping
// the router construction overhead.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface CompiledRoute {
  route: RouteDefinition;
  re: RegExp;
  paramNames: string[];
}

interface RouteCache {
  routes: RouteDefinition[];
  compiled: CompiledRoute[];
  db: Db;
  storage: StorageService;
  hyperdriveConnStr: string;
}

let routeCache: RouteCache | null = null;

// Convert an Express-style path pattern (with :param segments) to a RegExp.
function pathToRegex(path: string): { re: RegExp; paramNames: string[] } {
  const paramNames: string[] = [];
  const pattern = path
    .replace(/[$()*+.?[\\\]^{|}]/g, "\\$&")
    .replace(/:([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)/g, (_match, name: string) => {
      paramNames.push(name);
      return "([^/]+)";
    });
  return { re: new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`), paramNames };
}

function buildRouteCache(env: Env): RouteCache {
  const db = createHyperdriveDb(env.HYPERDRIVE);
  const r2Provider = new R2Provider(env.PAPERCLIP_STORAGE, {
    bucket: env.STORAGE_R2_BUCKET ?? "paperclip-storage",
    prefix: env.STORAGE_R2_PREFIX ?? "",
  });
  const storage = createCfStorageService(r2Provider) as unknown as StorageService;

  function ext(router: unknown, prefix: string): RouteDefinition[] {
    return extractRoutesFromRouter(router, prefix);
  }

  const routes: RouteDefinition[] = [
    ...ext(companyRoutes(db, storage), "/api/companies"),
    ...ext(agentRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
    ...ext(assetRoutes(db, storage), "/api"),
    ...ext(projectRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(issueRoutes(db, storage, {}), "/api"),
    ...ext(issueTreeControlRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(routineRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
    ...ext(environmentRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
    ...ext(executionWorkspaceRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(goalRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(approvalRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
    ...ext(secretRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(costRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
    ...ext(activityRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(dashboardRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(userProfileRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(sidecarBadgeRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(sidebarPreferenceRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(inboxDismissalRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(instanceSettingsRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(llmRoutes(db), "/api"),
    ...ext(authRoutes(db), "/api"),
  ];

  const compiled: CompiledRoute[] = routes.map((route) => ({
    route,
    ...pathToRegex(route.path),
  }));

  return { routes, compiled, db, storage, hyperdriveConnStr: env.HYPERDRIVE.connectionString };
}

function getRouteCache(env: Env): RouteCache {
  if (!routeCache || routeCache.hyperdriveConnStr !== env.HYPERDRIVE.connectionString) {
    routeCache = buildRouteCache(env);
    console.log(`[CF Worker] Built route cache: ${routeCache.routes.length} routes`);
  }
  return routeCache;
}

function getCompiledRoutes(env: Env) {
  const cache = getRouteCache(env);
  return { compiled: cache.compiled, db: cache.db, storage: cache.storage };
}</tool_use_error>

---
name: Cloudflare Workers local dev
description: CF Workers local dev is working; run pnpm dev:cf from root; key shims and patterns established
type: project
---

CF Workers local dev is working as of 2026-04-30 on branch feat/cloudflare-deployment.

**How to run:** `pnpm dev:cf` from root (or `pnpm dev` inside `packages/deploy-cloudflare`). Runs build-worker.mjs then `wrangler dev --no-bundle --local` on port 8787. Use `.dev.vars` with `DEPLOYMENT_MODE=local_trusted` to bypass auth.

**Key architecture decisions:**
- Custom esbuild bundler (build-worker.mjs) pre-bundles worker because wrangler 3 has no alias/external config
- Route handlers close over DB via service instances → DB must be rebuilt per-request (not cached across requests) to avoid CF Workers "Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request" error
- Route path regexps ARE cached (compiledPathCache module var) since they're stateless
- 229 routes compiled from Express-style route factories via express-router-bridge

**Shims in packages/deploy-cloudflare/src/shims/:**
- pino, pino-http → pino-shim.ts (console-backed logger)
- express → cf-express-shim.ts (zero-dep Router with param() no-op)
- server/src/middleware/logger.ts → server-logger-shim.ts (esbuild plugin intercept)
- server/src/version.ts → server-version-shim.ts (no createRequire)
- dotenv, multer → no-op shims (not needed in CF)
- node:http/https/net/tls/fs/etc. → stubs
- Banner polyfills: process.hrtime, process.cwd, process.chdir, process.exit

**Why:** Getting Node.js server codebase (Express, pino, multer, AWS SDK, postgres) to run in CF Workers which provides only a subset of Node.js APIs via nodejs_compat flag.

**Fixes made this session:**

- Shimmed `dotenv` and `multer` — both are CJS modules that do `require("path")` at init, which fails in CF Workers ESM

- Normalize trailing slashes in route paths and request URL (Express `router.get("/", ...)` + prefix `/api/companies` = `/api/companies/`, but requests arrive as `/api/companies`)
- **Per-request DB rebuild**: route handlers close over DB via service closures; CF Workers prohibits reusing TCP sockets across requests, so `buildRequestResources(env)` is called fresh per request. Route path regexps are cached separately.

338	  const pathname = rawPathname.length > 1 ? rawPathname.replace(/\/$/, "") : rawPathname;
339	  const method = c.req.method.toUpperCase();
340	
341	  for (const { route, re, paramNames } of compiled) {
342	    if (route.method !== method) continue;
343	    const match = re.exec(pathname);
344	    if (!match) continue;
345	
346	    // Build param map for this match
347	    const params: Record<string, string> = {};
348	    for (let i = 0; i < paramNames.length; i++) {
349	      params[paramNames[i]!] = match[i + 1]!;
350	    }
351	
352	    // Wrap ctx.param to return from our extracted params
353	    const actor = await resolveActorFromRequest(
354	      c.req.raw,
355	      db,
356	      {
357	        deploymentMode: c.env.DEPLOYMENT_MODE === "local_trusted"
358	          ? "local_trusted"
359	          : "authenticated",
360	      },
361	    );

363	    const ctx: import("../../../../server/src/http/types.js").RequestCtx = {
364	      method: c.req.method,
365	      url: new URL(c.req.url),
366	      headers: new Headers(c.req.raw.headers),
367	      json<T>(): Promise<T> { return c.req.json<T>(); },
368	      text(): Promise<string> { return c.req.text(); },
369	      param(name: string): string | undefined { return params[name]; },
370	      query(name: string): string | undefined { return c.req.query(name); },
371	      actor,
372	      db,
373	      storage,
374	    };
375	
376	    try {
377	      return await route.handler(ctx);
378	    } catch (err) {
379	      if (err instanceof HttpError) {
380	        return Response.json(
381	          { error: err.message, ...(err.details !== undefined ? { details: err.details } : {}) },
382	          { status: err.status },
383	        );
384	      }
385	      console.error(
386	        `[CF Worker] Unhandled error in ${route.method} ${route.path}: ${
387	          err instanceof Error ? err.stack ?? err.message : String(err)
388	        }`,
389	      );
390	      return Response.json({ error: "Internal Server Error" }, { status: 500 });
391	    }
392	  }

398	      code: "NOT_IMPLEMENTED",

442	  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
443	  async queue(batch: MessageBatch<unknown>, env: Env): Promise<void> {
444	    for (const message of batch.messages) {
445	      const body = message.body as Record<string, unknown>;
446	      const type = body?.type as string | undefined;
447	
448	      if (type === "plugin_job_dispatch") {
449	        const pluginJobId = body.pluginJobId as string;
450	        const pluginSlug = body.pluginSlug as string;
451	        const companyId = body.companyId as string;
452	        const executorMode = (body.executorMode as "sandbox_bridge" | "container") ?? "sandbox_bridge";
453	
454	        try {
455	          await env.PLUGIN_DISPATCH_WORKFLOW.create({
456	            id: `plugin-job-${pluginJobId}`,
457	            params: { pluginJobId, pluginSlug, companyId, executorMode },
458	          });
459	          message.ack();
460	        } catch (err) {
461	          console.error(
462	            `[Queue] Failed to start PluginDispatchWorkflow for job ${pluginJobId}: ${
463	              err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
464	            }`,
465	          );
466	          message.retry();
467	        }
468	        continue;
469	      }
470	
471	      if (type === "heartbeat_dispatch") {
472	        const agentId = body.agentId as string;
473	        const companyId = body.companyId as string;
474	        const runId = body.runId as string;
475	        const taskId = body.taskId as string | undefined;
476	
477	        try {
478	          await env.HEARTBEAT_WORKFLOW.create({
479	            id: `heartbeat-${runId}`,
480	            params: { agentId, companyId, runId, taskId },
481	          });
482	          message.ack();
483	        } catch (err) {
484	          console.error(
485	            `[Queue] Failed to start HeartbeatWorkflow for run ${runId}: ${
486	              err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
487	            }`,
488	          );
489	          message.retry();
490	        }
491	        continue;
492	      }
493	
494	      console.warn(`[Queue] Unknown message type: ${type}`);
495	      message.ack();
496	    }
497	  },

1	/**
2	 * Custom esbuild bundler for the Cloudflare Worker.
3	 *
4	 * Wrangler's built-in esbuild cannot mark specific packages as external or
5	 * alias individual modules, so we pre-bundle the worker here and point wrangler
6	 * to the output with --no-bundle.
7	 *
8	 * Two categories of problematic packages:
9	 *
10	 * 1. Available in CF Workers via nodejs_compat → mark as `external` so the CF
11	 *    runtime resolves them (node:crypto, node:stream, node:path, etc.)
12	 *
13	 * 2. NOT available in CF Workers (node:http, node:net, node:tls, node:fs, etc.)
14	 *    → alias to lightweight stubs bundled into the output. If the CF runtime tried
15	 *    to resolve these as externals it would crash on startup.
16	 *
17	 * Other stubs:
18	 *   - express → cf-express-shim (zero-dep Router that Express-router-bridge can walk)
19	 *   - embedded-postgres / @embedded-postgres/* → external (never called in CF)
20	 *   - jsdom → external (SVG sanitize path throws at runtime; acceptable for CF)

```text
1	/**
2	 * cf-express-shim.ts
3	 *
4	 * Zero-dependency replacement for `express` used in the Cloudflare Worker build.
5	 *
6	 * The server route factories call `Router()` and register routes with
7	 * router.get/post/patch/delete/put/use(). The Cloudflare adapter then walks
8	 * router.stack via express-router-bridge to extract the transport-agnostic
9	 * Handler functions (tagged with __handler by expressHandler).
10	 *
11	 * This shim replicates only the Express Router stack format that
12	 * express-router-bridge.ts expects:
13	 *   - Concrete routes: layer.route = { path, methods, stack: [{ handle }] }
14	 *   - Nested routers: layer.name = "router", layer.handle = nestedRouter,
15	 *                     layer.regexp = (Express-style prefix regexp)
16	 *
17	 * No Node.js built-ins are used — safe for the CF Workers runtime.
18	 */
19	
20	type MiddlewareFn = ((...args: unknown[]) => unknown) & { __handler?: unknown };
21	
22	interface RouteLayer {
23	  route: {
24	    path: string;
25	    methods: Record<string, boolean>;
26	    stack: Array<{ handle: MiddlewareFn }>;
27	  };
28	}
29	
30	interface RouterMountLayer {
31	  name: "router";
32	  handle: CfRouter;
33	  regexp: RegExp;
34	  keys: unknown[];
35	}
36	
37	type StackLayer = RouteLayer | RouterMountLayer;
38	
39	export interface CfRouter {
40	  stack: StackLayer[];
41	  get(path: string, ...fns: MiddlewareFn[]): this;
42	  post(path: string, ...fns: MiddlewareFn[]): this;
43	  patch(path: string, ...fns: MiddlewareFn[]): this;
44	  put(path: string, ...fns: MiddlewareFn[]): this;
45	  delete(path: string, ...fns: MiddlewareFn[]): this;
46	  use(prefix: string | CfRouter, ...rest: CfRouter[]): this;
47	  param(name: string, fn: MiddlewareFn): this;
48	}
49	
50	function buildRouteLayer(method: string, path: string, fns: MiddlewareFn[]): RouteLayer {
51	  return {
52	    route: {
53	      path,
54	      methods: { [method]: true },
55	      stack: fns.map((handle) => ({ handle })),
56	    },
57	  };
58	}
59	
60	function prefixToRegexp(prefix: string): RegExp {
61	  // Mirror the regexp format Express produces for app.use('/prefix', router):
62	  //   /^\\/prefix\/?(?=\/|$)/i
63	  // express-router-bridge.ts reverses this via extractPathFromLayerRegexp.
64	  const escaped = prefix.replace(/\//g, "\\/");
65	  return new RegExp(`^\${escaped}\\/?(?=\\/|$)`, "i");
66	}
67	
68	function createRouter(): CfRouter {
69	  const router: CfRouter = {
70	    stack: [],
71	    get(path, ...fns) { this.stack.push(buildRouteLayer("get", path, fns)); return this; },
72	    post(path, ...fns) { this.stack.push(buildRouteLayer("post", path, fns)); return this; },
73	    patch(path, ...fns) { this.stack.push(buildRouteLayer("patch", path, fns)); return this; },
74	    put(path, ...fns) { this.stack.push(buildRouteLayer("put", path, fns)); return this; },
75	    delete(path, ...fns) { this.stack.push(buildRouteLayer("delete", path, fns)); return this; },
76	    // param() is used for Express parameter pre-processing.
77	    // In CF Workers we only walk the stack statically, so this is a no-op.
78	    param(_name: string, _fn: MiddlewareFn) { return this; },
79	    use(prefix, ...rest) {
80	      if (typeof prefix === "string") {
81	        for (const nested of rest) {
82	          router.stack.push({
83	            name: "router",
84	            handle: nested,
85	            regexp: prefixToRegexp(prefix),
86	            keys: [],
87	          });
88	        }
89	      } else {
90	        // router.use(nestedRouter) — no prefix
91	        router.stack.push({
92	          name: "router",
93	          handle: prefix,
94	          regexp: prefixToRegexp(""),
95	          keys: [],
96	        });
97	      }
98	      return this;
99	    },
100	  };
101	  return router;
102	}
103	
104	// Default export matches express's export shape as used in the route files:
105	//   import { Router } from "express"
106	export const Router = createRouter;
107	
108	// Type-only re-exports so TypeScript is satisfied when route files do
109	//   import type { Request, Response, NextFunction } from "express"
110	// (type-only imports are erased at compile time, so no stubs needed)
111	export type Request = Record<string, unknown>;
112	export type Response = Record<string, unknown>;
113	export type NextFunction = () => void;
114	export type RequestHandler = MiddlewareFn;
115

1	import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/postgres-js";
2	import postgres from "postgres";
3	// Import the schema directly from the workspace source. The package.json exports
4	// map "./*" to "./src/*.ts", so "@paperclipai/db/schema" resolves to
5	// packages/db/src/schema.ts — but that file does not exist; the entry is
6	// packages/db/src/schema/index.ts. We use a relative path to be explicit and
7	// avoid relying on bundler heuristics for directory index resolution.
8	import * as schema from "../../../db/src/schema/index.js";
9	import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
10	
11	/**
12	 * Minimal interface that matches the Cloudflare Hyperdrive binding shape.
13	 * The full type is `Hyperdrive` from `@cloudflare/workers-types`, but we
14	 * declare a local structural equivalent so this file compiles without
15	 * requiring the workers-types package at import time.
16	 */
17	export interface HyperdriveBinding {
18	  /** The connection string Cloudflare injects — points to the Hyperdrive proxy. */
19	  connectionString: string;
20	}
21	
22	/**
23	 * Creates a Drizzle `Db` instance backed by Cloudflare Hyperdrive.
24	 *
25	 * Hyperdrive terminates the Postgres connection pool near the Worker and
26	 * forwards queries to the upstream Neon/Postgres database over a long-lived
27	 * TCP connection. The `postgres-js` driver is compatible with the Workers
28	 * `nodejs_compat` flag, which provides a polyfilled TCP socket layer.
29	 *
30	 * Pool size is capped at 5 — each Worker invocation is short-lived so a
31	 * large pool wastes Hyperdrive connection slots.
32	 *
33	 * @param hyperdrive - The Hyperdrive binding from the Worker `Env`.
34	 */
35	export function createHyperdriveDb(hyperdrive: HyperdriveBinding): Db {
36	  // max: 5 keeps connection usage low across concurrent invocations.
37	  // prepare: false disables prepared-statement caching because Hyperdrive
38	  // routes across multiple upstream connections and cannot share PS state.
39	  const sql = postgres(hyperdrive.connectionString, {
40	    max: 5,
41	    prepare: false,
42	  });
43	  // drizzle-orm's postgres-js adapter returns a type that is structurally
44	  // identical to the `Db` exported from @paperclipai/db. The cast via
45	  // `unknown` is necessary only because the generic parameters differ at
46	  // the type level; the runtime shapes are identical.
47	  return drizzle(sql, { schema }) as unknown as Db;
48	}

```text
1	/**
2	 * express-router-bridge.ts
3	 *
4	 * Walks an Express Router's internal `.stack` to extract route definitions that
5	 * carry a `__handler` tag (set by the tagged `expressHandler` wrapper in
6	 * `server/src/http/express-adapter.ts`). The extracted definitions are the
7	 * transport-agnostic `Handler` functions that can be mounted directly on the
8	 * Hono app without pulling in any Node-specific Express machinery.
9	 *
10	 * This file is Workers-safe: it imports only type-level dependencies from the
11	 * server package and performs no Node-only I/O at runtime. The Express Router
12	 * object is passed in as an opaque `unknown` and interrogated structurally.
13	 */
14	
15	import type { Handler, RouteDefinition } from "../../../../server/src/http/types.js";
16	
17	/** A function that may carry the `__handler` tag set by `expressHandler`. */
18	type TaggedFn = ((...args: unknown[]) => unknown) & { __handler?: Handler };
19	
20	/**
21	 * Shape of a single layer inside an Express Router's internal `.stack` array.
22	 * These are not publicly typed by Express, so we define a local structural
23	 * interface that matches what Express 4.x and 5.x actually produce at runtime.
24	 */
25	interface RouterLayer {
26	  /** Present when this layer is a concrete route (app.get / app.post / etc.). */
27	  route?: {
28	    path: string;
29	    methods: Record<string, boolean>;
30	    stack: Array<{ handle: TaggedFn }>;
31	  };
32	  /** "router" when this layer wraps a nested Router (app.use('/prefix', router)). */
33	  name?: string;
34	  /** The nested Router object when name === "router". */
35	  handle?: { stack?: RouterLayer[] };
36	  /** The compiled regexp Express stores for the mount prefix. */
37	  regexp?: RegExp;
38	  /** Named capture groups extracted from the regexp. */
39	  keys?: Array<{ name: string }>;
40	}
41	
42	/**
43	 * Reverse-engineers the mount prefix Express stored as a regexp back into a
44	 * plain path string.
45	 *
46	 * Express generates regexps like:
47	 *   `/^\/companies\/?(?=\/|$)/i`
48	 * from a prefix like `/companies`. We extract the literal path segment from
49	 * the known pattern so we can rebuild full route paths for nested routers.
50	 *
51	 * Returns an empty string when the layer has no extractable prefix (e.g. the
52	 * root-mounted catch-all).
53	 */
54	function extractPathFromLayerRegexp(layer: RouterLayer): string {
55	  if (!layer.regexp) return "";
56	  const src = layer.regexp.source;
57	  // Pattern produced by Express for a simple path prefix like "/companies":
58	  //   ^\\/companies\\/?(?=\\/|$)
59	  const m = src.match(/^\^\\\/(.+?)\\\/\?\(\?=\\\/\|\$\)/);
60	  if (m) return "/" + m[1].replace(/\\\//g, "/");
61	  return "";
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Recursively walks an Express Router's `.stack` and returns all
66	 * `RouteDefinition` objects whose innermost handler carries a `__handler` tag.
67	 *
68	 * @param routerObj - The Express `Router` instance (typed as `unknown` to avoid
69	 *   importing Express at the call site, which would pull in Node-only types).
70	 * @param prefix - The path prefix accumulated from outer `app.use()` calls.
71	 */
72	export function extractRoutesFromRouter(
73	  routerObj: unknown,
74	  prefix = "",
75	): RouteDefinition[] {
76	  const router = routerObj as { stack?: RouterLayer[] };
77	  const defs: RouteDefinition[] = [];
78	
79	  for (const layer of router.stack ?? []) {
80	    if (layer.route) {
81	      // This layer is a concrete route (GET /foo, POST /bar, etc.)
82	      const rawPath = prefix + layer.route.path;
83	      // Normalize: strip trailing slash except for a bare "/"
84	      const path = rawPath.length > 1 && rawPath.endsWith("/") ? rawPath.slice(0, -1) : rawPath;
85	      for (const [method, enabled] of Object.entries(layer.route.methods)) {
86	        if (!enabled) continue;
87	        for (const rl of layer.route.stack) {
88	          if (rl.handle.__handler) {
89	            defs.push({
90	              method: method.toUpperCase() as RouteDefinition["method"],
91	              path,
92	              handler: rl.handle.__handler,
93	            });
94	            break; // Only take the first tagged handler per method
95	          }
96	        }
97	      }
98	    } else if (layer.name === "router" && layer.handle?.stack) {
99	      // This layer is a nested Router mounted via app.use('/prefix', router)
100	      const nested = extractPathFromLayerRegexp(layer);
101	      defs.push(...extractRoutesFromRouter(layer.handle, prefix + nested));
102	    }
103	  }
104	
105	  return defs;
106	}
107

/**
 * resolve-actor.ts — Cloudflare Workers port of the Express actorMiddleware.
 *
 * Resolves the authenticated actor from a Web API `Request` object without
 * depending on any Node-only modules (`node:crypto`, Express types, etc.).
 *
 * SHA-256 hashing uses the Web Crypto API (`crypto.subtle`) which is available
 * in both the Workers runtime and modern Node.js (>= 19 with global `crypto`).
 *
 * BetterAuth session lookup is skipped for the Workers deployment — the CF
 * Worker authenticates via Bearer tokens (agent JWTs, agent API keys, and
 * board API keys). UI sessions that rely on HTTP-only cookies must go through
 * BetterAuth's own `/api/auth/*` handler, which is mounted separately.
 */

import { and, eq, isNull } from "drizzle-orm";
import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
import { agentApiKeys, agents, authUsers, boardApiKeys, companyMemberships, instanceUserRoles } from "@paperclipai/db";
import type { ActorContext } from "../../../../server/src/http/types.js";
import { verifyLocalAgentJwt } from "../../../../server/src/agent-auth-jwt.js";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Internal helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** SHA-256 hash a token using the Web Crypto API, returning a lowercase hex string. */
async function hashToken(token: string): Promise<string> {
  const buf = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", new TextEncoder().encode(token));
  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(buf))
    .map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
    .join("");
}

/**
 * Resolve the board actor memberships for a given userId.
 * Queries `companyMemberships` and `instanceUserRoles` in parallel.
 */
async function resolveBoardAccess(db: Db, userId: string) {
  const [user, memberships, adminRole] = await Promise.all([
    db
      .select({ id: authUsers.id, name: authUsers.name, email: authUsers.email })
      .from(authUsers)
      .where(eq(authUsers.id, userId))
      .then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null),
    db
      .select({
        companyId: companyMemberships.companyId,
        membershipRole: companyMemberships.membershipRole,
        status: companyMemberships.status,
      })

**CRITICAL**

1. `buildRequestResources` creates a new `postgres()` pool on every request — connections are never closed, causing unbounded connection exhaustion under load.
2. The two R2 upload handlers each call `buildRequestResources` independently, creating a second pool on the same request — doubling the leak for any upload.

**HIGH**

3. `getCompiledRoutes` is a dead pass-through wrapper around `buildRequestResources`; the routing comment above it documents caching that doesn't exist — the cache only covers regex patterns, not service instances.
4. `compiledPathCache` assumes route order is stable across isolate lifetimes; if any route factory changes its output order between cold starts the regex-to-handler pairing silently misroutes requests.
5. Queue message bodies are cast directly to `Record<string, unknown>` with no schema validation — a malformed message can pass garbage field values into Workflow `params` with no error surface until runtime.
6. `.dev.vars` is tracked by git (not in `.gitignore`) and contains `SIDECAR_API_KEY=dev-local`; establishes a pattern of committing secrets files.
7. `jsdom` is marked external in `CF_PROVIDED_BUILTINS` (so CF runtime tries to resolve it) but is not available in CF — the build comment says "acceptable" but assets route lazy-imports it, which fails silently only at runtime on that path.

**MEDIUM**

8. `deploymentMode` ternary is duplicated verbatim in three separate locations (lines 266, 302, 357–358) — a single helper function would make it impossible to desync.
9. `skillsService` and `instructionsService` are instantiated per-request inside the `fetch` handler then immediately voided — dead construction that wastes CPU and obscures intent.
10. `SidecarClient` is also instantiated per-request in `fetch` but never injected anywhere — it isn't passed to the route machinery.
11. `Env` interface is defined inline in `api.ts` alongside 500 lines of application logic — should be a separate types file so other modules can import it without pulling in all routes.
12. `import.meta.url` define is applied globally across the entire bundle, not scoped to `db/src/client.ts`; this could mask legitimate `import.meta.url` usages in other bundled code.
13. `createSetupApp(c.env)` is called on every request matching `/setup` or `/setup/*` — a new app instance per request rather than a module-level singleton.
14. `compatibility_date = "2024-09-23"` is over a year stale; new CF runtime fixes and security patches gated behind newer dates are unavailable.
15. No `.dev.vars.example` template exists; contributors have no documented reference for required local overrides.

**LOW**

16. `console.log("[Cron] Budget check -- not yet implemented")` and the DB backup equivalent emit to production logs on every hourly/daily cron fire.
17. `console.log("[CF Worker] Compiled N route patterns")` fires on every cold start — useful during development but noise in production.
18. `notAvailable` and `notAvailableSync` in `node-fs.ts` are identical functions with different names — one is sufficient.
19. `node-fs.ts` inlines a `promises` namespace that duplicates `node-fs-promises.ts`; two sources of truth for the same stubs.

22. `pool.max: 5` comment in `hyperdrive.ts` says "short-lived invocations" but `max: 5` per cold-start multiplied by concurrent isolates can still exhaust Hyperdrive's upstream slot limit.

308	    const issueRow = await db.select({ id: issues.id, companyId: issues.companyId })
309	      .from(issues).where(eq(issues.id, issueId)).then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null);
310	    if (!issueRow) throw notFound("Issue not found");
311	
312	    if (!actor) throw forbidden("Authentication required");
313	    if (actor.type === "board" && !actor.isInstanceAdmin && !actor.companyIds?.includes(issueRow.companyId)) {

315	    }
316	    if (actor.type === "agent" && actor.companyId !== issueRow.companyId) {

320	    const body = c.req.raw.body;
321	    if (!body) throw badRequest("Empty request body");
322	    const filename = (c.req.header("x-filename") ?? "attachment").replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/g, "_");

329	    return c.json({ error: "Internal Server Error" }, 500);
330	  }

1	import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/postgres-js";
2	import postgres from "postgres";
3	// Import the schema directly from the workspace source. The package.json exports
4	// map "./*" to "./src/*.ts", so "@paperclipai/db/schema" resolves to
5	// packages/db/src/schema.ts — but that file does not exist; the entry is
6	// packages/db/src/schema/index.ts. We use a relative path to be explicit and
7	// avoid relying on bundler heuristics for directory index resolution.
8	import * as schema from "../../../db/src/schema/index.js";
9	import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
10	
11	/**
12	 * Minimal interface that matches the Cloudflare Hyperdrive binding shape.
13	 * The full type is `Hyperdrive` from `@cloudflare/workers-types`, but we
14	 * declare a local structural equivalent so this file compiles without
15	 * requiring the workers-types package at import time.
16	 */
17	export interface HyperdriveBinding {
18	  /** The connection string Cloudflare injects — points to the Hyperdrive proxy. */
19	  connectionString: string;
20	}
21	
22	/**
23	 * Creates a Drizzle `Db` instance backed by Cloudflare Hyperdrive.
24	 *
25	 * Hyperdrive terminates the Postgres connection pool near the Worker and
26	 * forwards queries to the upstream Neon/Postgres database over a long-lived
27	 * TCP connection. The `postgres-js` driver is compatible with the Workers
28	 * `nodejs_compat` flag, which provides a polyfilled TCP socket layer.
29	 *
30	 * Pool size is capped at 5 — each Worker invocation is short-lived so a
31	 * large pool wastes Hyperdrive connection slots.
32	 *
33	 * @param hyperdrive - The Hyperdrive binding from the Worker `Env`.
34	 */
35	export function createHyperdriveDb(hyperdrive: HyperdriveBinding): Db {
36	  // max: 5 keeps connection usage low across concurrent invocations.
37	  // prepare: false disables prepared-statement caching because Hyperdrive
38	  // routes across multiple upstream connections and cannot share PS state.
39	  const sql = postgres(hyperdrive.connectionString, {
40	    max: 5,
41	    prepare: false,
42	  });
43	  // drizzle-orm's postgres-js adapter returns a type that is structurally
44	  // identical to the `Db` exported from @paperclipai/db. The cast via
45	  // `unknown` is necessary only because the generic parameters differ at
46	  // the type level; the runtime shapes are identical.
47	  return drizzle(sql, { schema }) as unknown as Db;
48	}

11	 *    runtime resolves them (node:crypto, node:stream, node:path, etc.)

**Architectural Impact: High** (connection-leak pattern is per-request in production)

**CRITICAL**

1. `buildRequestResources` creates a new `postgres()` pool on every request — connections are never closed, causing unbounded connection exhaustion under load.
2. The two R2 upload handlers each call `buildRequestResources` independently, creating a second pool on the same request — doubling the leak for any upload.

**HIGH**

3. `getCompiledRoutes` is a dead pass-through wrapper around `buildRequestResources`; the routing comment above it documents caching that doesn't exist — the cache only covers regex patterns, not service instances.
4. `compiledPathCache` assumes route order is stable across isolate lifetimes; if any route factory changes its output order between cold starts the regex-to-handler pairing silently misroutes requests.
5. Queue message bodies are cast directly to `Record<string, unknown>` with no schema validation — a malformed message can pass garbage field values into Workflow `params` with no error surface until runtime.
6. `.dev.vars` is tracked by git (not in `.gitignore`) and contains `SIDECAR_API_KEY=dev-local`; establishes a pattern of committing secrets files.
7. `jsdom` is marked external in `CF_PROVIDED_BUILTINS` (so CF runtime tries to resolve it) but is not available in CF — the build comment says "acceptable" but assets route lazy-imports it, which fails silently only at runtime on that path.

10. `SidecarClient` is also instantiated per-request in `fetch` but never injected anywhere — it isn't passed to the route machinery.
11. `Env` interface is defined inline in `api.ts` alongside 500 lines of application logic — should be a separate types file so other modules can import it without pulling in all routes.
12. `import.meta.url` define is applied globally across the entire bundle, not scoped to `db/src/client.ts`; this could mask legitimate `import.meta.url` usages in other bundled code.
13. `createSetupApp(c.env)` is called on every request matching `/setup` or `/setup/*` — a new app instance per request rather than a module-level singleton.
14. `compatibility_date = "2024-09-23"` is over a year stale; new CF runtime fixes and security patches gated behind newer dates are unavailable.
15. No `.dev.vars.example` template exists; contributors have no documented reference for required local overrides.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
- **Custom esbuild bundler** (`build-worker.mjs`): pre-bundles the worker because wrangler 3's built-in esbuild has no `alias`/`external` per-package config
- **CF Workers ESM**: no global `require`, no TCP socket reuse across requests, no Node.js file system
- **Per-request DB pattern**: route handlers close over service instances which close over the postgres `Db`; CF Workers prohibits reusing TCP sockets across requests, so DB + route handlers must be rebuilt per-request
- **`compiledPathCache`**: module-level cache for route path regexps (stateless, safe to cache); route handler closures are NOT cached
- **Express Router bridge**: `extractRoutesFromRouter` walks the CF express shim's `.stack` to extract `__handler`-tagged functions (transport-agnostic handlers)
- **CF express shim**: zero-dep Router replacement that produces the same `.stack` format that `express-router-bridge.ts` reads
- **Node.js API shims**: CJS-safe stubs for node:http, node:https, node:net, node:tls, node:fs, node:fs/promises, node:child_process, node:os, node:http2, node:readline
- **pino shim**: full CF-safe console-backed pino replacement (no worker_threads, no events)
- **esbuild plugin for path interception**: since `alias` only works for bare module names, a plugin with `onResolve` hooks intercepts server source files by resolving `args.resolveDir + args.path` against known absolute paths
- **Banner polyfill**: injects `process.hrtime`, `process.cwd`, `process.chdir`, `process.exit` before any module initialization
- **`platform: "node"`**: was changed from `"neutral"` to get proper CJS require→import interop in esbuild
- **`DEPLOYMENT_MODE=local_trusted`**: bypasses auth resolution and setup KV gate for local dev

4. Errors and fixes:

- **`Invalid alias name: "/path/to/logger.ts"`**: esbuild `alias` only accepts bare module names. Fixed by using an esbuild plugin with `onResolve` hooks that match by resolving the full absolute path.

- **Plugin filter not catching relative imports**: Filter `/\/server\/src\/version.../` didn't match `./version`. Fixed by resolving `path.resolve(args.resolveDir, args.path)` and comparing against the target absolute path.

- **`Invalid specifier path: ../package.json`**: `server/src/version.ts` uses `createRequire` + `require("../package.json")`. Fixed by creating `server-version-shim.ts` and intercepting it with the plugin.

- **Plugin shim path wrong**: Initial plugin constructed path as `SHIMS/middleware/logger.ts` instead of `SHIMS/server-logger-shim.ts`. Fixed by separating `serverRelPath` (for matching) from `shimFile` (for destination filename).

- **`Dynamic require of "path" is not supported` (dotenv)**: dotenv is CJS and calls `__require("path")` at module init; CF Workers ESM has no global `require`. Fixed by creating `dotenv-shim.ts` and aliasing `"dotenv"` to it.

- **Same error from multer chain**: multer → type-is → mime-types all use `require("path")`. Fixed by creating `multer-shim.ts` and aliasing `"multer"` to it.

- **`process.cwd is not a function`**: CF Workers global `process` doesn't have `cwd`. Fixed by adding `process.cwd`, `process.chdir`, `process.exit` to the banner polyfill in build-worker.mjs.

- **`router.param is not a function`**: CF express shim missing `.param()`. Fixed by adding no-op `param(_name, _fn) { return this; }`.

- **302 redirect to `/setup` for all routes**: Setup gate checks `PAPERCLIP_KV.get("SETUP_COMPLETED")` which is empty in Miniflare. Fixed by adding `if (c.env.DEPLOYMENT_MODE === "local_trusted") return next();`.

- **501 for `/api/companies`**: Route path was `/api/companies/` but request was `/api/companies`. Fixed in two places:
  1. `express-router-bridge.ts`: strip trailing slash from extracted paths
  2. Catch-all handler: normalize request pathname with `rawPathname.replace(/\/$/, "")`

- **`Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request`**: Cached postgres connection from request 1 reused in request 2. Fixed by removing the route cache and rebuilding DB + service instances + route handlers on every request. Only the compiled path regexps (`compiledPathCache`) are cached since they're stateless.

131	// Convert an Express-style path pattern (with :param segments) to a RegExp.
132	function pathToRegex(path: string): { re: RegExp; paramNames: string[] } {
133	  const paramNames: string[] = [];
134	  const pattern = path
135	    .replace(/[$()*+.?[\\\]^{|}]/g, "\\$&")
136	    .replace(/:([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)/g, (_match, name: string) => {
137	      paramNames.push(name);
138	      return "([^/]+)";
139	    });
140	  return { re: new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`), paramNames };
141	}

317	      throw forbidden("No access to this company");
318	    }
319	
320	    const body = c.req.raw.body;
321	    if (!body) throw badRequest("Empty request body");
322	    const filename = (c.req.header("x-filename") ?? "attachment").replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/g, "_");
323	    const key = `issues/${issueRow.companyId}/${issueId}/attachments/${filename}`;
324	    await env.PAPERCLIP_STORAGE.put(key, body, { httpMetadata: { contentType: c.req.header("content-type") ?? "application/octet-stream" } });
325	    return c.json({ ok: true, key, filename });
326	  } catch (err) {
327	    if (err instanceof HttpError) return c.json({ error: err.message }, err.status as 400 | 403 | 404);
328	    console.error("[CF Worker] POST /api/issues/:issueId/attachments/upload", err);
329	    return c.json({ error: "Internal Server Error" }, 500);
330	  }
331	});
332	
333	// Main API catch-all -- manual routing through cached route definitions
334	app.all("/api/*", async (c) => {
335	  const { compiled, db, storage } = getCompiledRoutes(c.env);
336	  // Strip trailing slash so /api/companies/ matches /api/companies routes.
337	  const rawPathname = new URL(c.req.url).pathname;
338	  const pathname = rawPathname.length > 1 ? rawPathname.replace(/\/$/, "") : rawPathname;
339	  const method = c.req.method.toUpperCase();
340	
341	  for (const { route, re, paramNames } of compiled) {
342	    if (route.method !== method) continue;
343	    const match = re.exec(pathname);
344	    if (!match) continue;
345	
346	    // Build param map for this match
347	    const params: Record<string, string> = {};
348	    for (let i = 0; i < paramNames.length; i++) {
349	      params[paramNames[i]!] = match[i + 1]!;
350	    }
351	
352	    // Wrap ctx.param to return from our extracted params
353	    const actor = await resolveActorFromRequest(
354	      c.req.raw,
355	      db,
356	      {
357	        deploymentMode: c.env.DEPLOYMENT_MODE === "local_trusted"
358	          ? "local_trusted"
359	          : "authenticated",
360	      },
361	    );
362	
363	    const ctx: import("../../../../server/src/http/types.js").RequestCtx = {
364	      method: c.req.method,
365	      url: new URL(c.req.url),
366	      headers: new Headers(c.req.raw.headers),
367	      json<T>(): Promise<T> { return c.req.json<T>(); },
368	      text(): Promise<string> { return c.req.text(); },
369	      param(name: string): string | undefined { return params[name]; },
370	      query(name: string): string | undefined { return c.req.query(name); },
371	      actor,
372	      db,
373	      storage,
374	    };
375	
376	    try {
377	      return await route.handler(ctx);
378	    } catch (err) {
379	      if (err instanceof HttpError) {
380	        return Response.json(
381	          { error: err.message, ...(err.details !== undefined ? { details: err.details } : {}) },
382	          { status: err.status },
383	        );
384	      }
385	      console.error(
386	        `[CF Worker] Unhandled error in ${route.method} ${route.path}: ${
387	          err instanceof Error ? err.stack ?? err.message : String(err)
388	        }`,
389	      );
390	      return Response.json({ error: "Internal Server Error" }, { status: 500 });
391	    }
392	  }
393	
394	  // No route matched
395	  return c.json(
396	    {
397	      error: "This API route is not available in the Cloudflare Workers deployment.",
398	      code: "NOT_IMPLEMENTED",
399	    },
400	    501,
401	  );
402	});

411	</body></html>`,
412	  ),

421	    // Boot the Cloudflare implementations on first request (idempotent).
422	    bootCloudflare(env);
423

427	    const sidecar = new SidecarClient({

443	  async queue(batch: MessageBatch<unknown>, env: Env): Promise<void> {
444	    for (const message of batch.messages) {
445	      const body = message.body as Record<string, unknown>;
446	      const type = body?.type as string | undefined;
447

449	        const pluginJobId = body.pluginJobId as string;
450	        const pluginSlug = body.pluginSlug as string;
451	        const companyId = body.companyId as string;
452	        const executorMode = (body.executorMode as "sandbox_bridge" | "container") ?? "sandbox_bridge";
453	
454	        try {

456	            id: `plugin-job-${pluginJobId}`,
457	            params: { pluginJobId, pluginSlug, companyId, executorMode },
458	          });
459	          message.ack();
460	        } catch (err) {

463	              err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
464	            }`,
465	          );
466	          message.retry();
467	        }
468	        continue;
469	      }
470	
471	      if (type === "heartbeat_dispatch") {
472	        const agentId = body.agentId as string;
473	        const companyId = body.companyId as string;
474	        const runId = body.runId as string;
475	        const taskId = body.taskId as string | undefined;
476	
477	        try {

479	            id: `heartbeat-${runId}`,

481	          });

483	        } catch (err) {
484	          console.error(

486	              err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
487	            }`,
488	          );
489	          message.retry();
490	        }
491	        continue;
492	      }
493	
494	      console.warn(`[Queue] Unknown message type: ${type}`);
495	      message.ack();
496	    }

1	import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/postgres-js";
2	import postgres from "postgres";
3	// Import the schema directly from the workspace source. The package.json exports
4	// map "./*" to "./src/*.ts", so "@paperclipai/db/schema" resolves to
5	// packages/db/src/schema.ts — but that file does not exist; the entry is
6	// packages/db/src/schema/index.ts. We use a relative path to be explicit and
7	// avoid relying on bundler heuristics for directory index resolution.
8	import * as schema from "../../../db/src/schema/index.js";
9	import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
10	
11	/**
12	 * Minimal interface that matches the Cloudflare Hyperdrive binding shape.
13	 * The full type is `Hyperdrive` from `@cloudflare/workers-types`, but we
14	 * declare a local structural equivalent so this file compiles without
15	 * requiring the workers-types package at import time.
16	 */
17	export interface HyperdriveBinding {
18	  /** The connection string Cloudflare injects — points to the Hyperdrive proxy. */
19	  connectionString: string;
20	}
21	
22	/**
23	 * Creates a Drizzle `Db` instance backed by Cloudflare Hyperdrive.
24	 *
25	 * Hyperdrive terminates the Postgres connection pool near the Worker and
26	 * forwards queries to the upstream Neon/Postgres database over a long-lived
27	 * TCP connection. The `postgres-js` driver is compatible with the Workers
28	 * `nodejs_compat` flag, which provides a polyfilled TCP socket layer.
29	 *
30	 * Pool size is capped at 5 — each Worker invocation is short-lived so a
31	 * large pool wastes Hyperdrive connection slots.
32	 *
33	 * @param hyperdrive - The Hyperdrive binding from the Worker `Env`.
34	 */
35	export function createHyperdriveDb(hyperdrive: HyperdriveBinding): Db {
36	  // max: 5 keeps connection usage low across concurrent invocations.
37	  // prepare: false disables prepared-statement caching because Hyperdrive
38	  // routes across multiple upstream connections and cannot share PS state.
39	  const sql = postgres(hyperdrive.connectionString, {
40	    max: 5,
41	    prepare: false,
42	  });
43	  // drizzle-orm's postgres-js adapter returns a type that is structurally
44	  // identical to the `Db` exported from @paperclipai/db. The cast via
45	  // `unknown` is necessary only because the generic parameters differ at
46	  // the type level; the runtime shapes are identical.
47	  return drizzle(sql, { schema }) as unknown as Db;
48	}
49
