/**
 * resolve-actor.ts — Cloudflare Workers port of the Express actorMiddleware.
 *
 * Resolves the authenticated actor from a Web API `Request` object without
 * depending on any Node-only modules (`node:crypto`, Express types, etc.).
 *
 * SHA-256 hashing uses the Web Crypto API (`crypto.subtle`) which is available
 * in both the Workers runtime and modern Node.js (>= 19 with global `crypto`).
 *
 * BetterAuth session lookup is skipped for the Workers deployment — the CF
 * Worker authenticates via Bearer tokens (agent JWTs, agent API keys, and
 * board API keys). UI sessions that rely on HTTP-only cookies must go through
 * BetterAuth's own `/api/auth/*` handler, which is mounted separately.
 */

import { and, eq, isNull } from "drizzle-orm";
import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
import { agentApiKeys, agents, authUsers, boardApiKeys, companyMemberships, instanceUserRoles } from "@paperclipai/db";
import type { ActorContext } from "../../../../server/src/http/types.js";
import { verifyLocalAgentJwt } from "../../../../server/src/agent-auth-jwt.js";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Internal helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** SHA-256 hash a token using the Web Crypto API, returning a lowercase hex string. */
async function hashToken(token: string): Promise<string> {
  const buf = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", new TextEncoder().encode(token));
  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(buf))
    .map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
    .join("");
}

/**
 * Resolve the board actor memberships for a given userId.
 * Queries `companyMemberships` and `instanceUserRoles` in parallel.
 */
async function resolveBoardAccess(db: Db, userId: string) {
  const [user, memberships, adminRole] = await Promise.all([
    db
      .select({ id: authUsers.id, name: authUsers.name, email: authUsers.email })
      .from(authUsers)
      .where(eq(authUsers.id, userId))
      .then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null),
    db
      .select({
        companyId: companyMemberships.companyId,
        membershipRole: companyMemberships.membershipRole,
        status: companyMemberships.status,
      })
      .from(companyMemberships)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(companyMemberships.principalType, "user"),
          eq(companyMemberships.principalId, userId),
          eq(companyMemberships.status, "active"),
        ),
      ),
    db
      .select({ id: instanceUserRoles.id })
      .from(instanceUserRoles)
      .where(and(eq(instanceUserRoles.userId, userId), eq(instanceUserRoles.role, "instance_admin")))
      .then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null),
  ]);

  return {
    user,
    companyIds: memberships.map((row) => row.companyId),
    memberships,
    isInstanceAdmin: Boolean(adminRole),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Public API
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export type DeploymentMode = "local_trusted" | "authenticated";

/**
 * Resolves the actor from the incoming Web API `Request`.
 *
 * Resolution order:
 * 1. `local_trusted` mode → always returns a local implicit board actor (no DB
 *    queries needed).
 * 2. `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header:
 *    a. Board API key (pcp_board_* tokens stored in `boardApiKeys`).
 *    b. Agent API key (hash stored in `agentApiKeys`).
 *    c. Agent JWT (HMAC-signed token; verified without DB lookup).
 * 3. No Bearer token or unrecognised token → returns `null` (unauthenticated).
 *
 * Note: Cookie-based BetterAuth sessions are not resolved here. The Cloudflare
 * deployment uses the BetterAuth `/api/auth/*` handler separately, and the UI
 * exchanges the session cookie for a Board API key on first visit.
 */
export async function resolveActorFromRequest(
  request: Request,
  db: Db,
  opts: { deploymentMode: DeploymentMode },
): Promise<ActorContext | null> {
  // 1. Local trusted mode — skip all auth checks.
  if (opts.deploymentMode === "local_trusted") {
    return {
      type: "board",
      source: "local_implicit",
      userId: "local-board",
      userName: "Local Board",
      userEmail: null,
      isInstanceAdmin: true,
    };
  }

  const runIdHeader = request.headers.get("x-paperclip-run-id") ?? undefined;

  // 2. Bearer token
  const authHeader = request.headers.get("authorization") ?? "";
  if (!authHeader.toLowerCase().startsWith("bearer ")) {
    return null;
  }

  const token = authHeader.slice("bearer ".length).trim();
  if (!token) return null;

  // 2a. Board API key — stored as pcp_board_* with a hash in boardApiKeys table.
  const tokenHash = await hashToken(token);
  const boardKey = await db
    .select()
    .from(boardApiKeys)
    .where(and(eq(boardApiKeys.keyHash, tokenHash), isNull(boardApiKeys.revokedAt)))
    .then((rows) => {
      const now = new Date();
      return rows.find((row) => !row.expiresAt || row.expiresAt.getTime() > now.getTime()) ?? null;
    });

  if (boardKey) {
    const access = await resolveBoardAccess(db, boardKey.userId);
    if (access.user) {
      // Touch lastUsedAt asynchronously — don't block the response.
      void db
        .update(boardApiKeys)
        .set({ lastUsedAt: new Date() })
        .where(eq(boardApiKeys.id, boardKey.id));

      return {
        type: "board",
        source: "board_key",
        userId: boardKey.userId,
        userName: access.user.name ?? null,
        userEmail: access.user.email ?? null,
        companyIds: access.companyIds,
        memberships: access.memberships.map((m) => ({ ...m, membershipRole: m.membershipRole ?? "" })),
        isInstanceAdmin: access.isInstanceAdmin,
        keyId: boardKey.id,
        runId: runIdHeader,
      };
    }
  }

  // 2b. Agent API key — hash stored in agentApiKeys.
  const agentKey = await db
    .select()
    .from(agentApiKeys)
    .where(and(eq(agentApiKeys.keyHash, tokenHash), isNull(agentApiKeys.revokedAt)))
    .then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null);

  if (agentKey) {
    const agentRecord = await db
      .select()
      .from(agents)
      .where(eq(agents.id, agentKey.agentId))
      .then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null);

    if (
      agentRecord &&
      agentRecord.status !== "terminated" &&
      agentRecord.status !== "pending_approval"
    ) {
      // Touch lastUsedAt asynchronously.
      void db
        .update(agentApiKeys)
        .set({ lastUsedAt: new Date() })
        .where(eq(agentApiKeys.id, agentKey.id));

      return {
        type: "agent",
        source: "agent_key",
        agentId: agentKey.agentId,
        companyId: agentKey.companyId,
        keyId: agentKey.id,
        runId: runIdHeader,
      };
    }
    // Key exists but agent is terminated/pending — fall through to return null.
    return null;
  }

  // 2c. Agent JWT — verified with HMAC secret; no DB lookup needed for
  //     the signature, but we validate the agent still exists and is active.
  const claims = verifyLocalAgentJwt(token);
  if (claims) {
    const agentRecord = await db
      .select()
      .from(agents)
      .where(eq(agents.id, claims.sub))
      .then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null);

    if (
      agentRecord &&
      agentRecord.companyId === claims.company_id &&
      agentRecord.status !== "terminated" &&
      agentRecord.status !== "pending_approval"
    ) {
      return {
        type: "agent",
        source: "agent_jwt",
        agentId: claims.sub,
        companyId: claims.company_id,
        runId: runIdHeader ?? claims.run_id ?? undefined,
      };
    }
  }

  // Unrecognised or invalid token.
  return null;
}

/**
 * cf-express-bridge.ts
 *
 * Bridges raw Express route handlers (req, res, next) to the transport-agnostic
 * Handler type used by the CF Workers route registry.
 *
 * Route factories in the server package (access.ts, company-skills.ts) use raw
 * Express handlers instead of the expressHandler adapter, making them invisible
 * to extractRoutesFromRouter. This bridge:
 *
 *   1. Walks the Express router stack to find untagged routes.
 *   2. Wraps each raw handler chain as a transport-agnostic Handler.
 *   3. Inside each Handler, builds a minimal mock req/res, runs the Express
 *      middleware chain, and resolves to the captured Web Response.
 *
 * Only the subset of Express req/res API used by the server's route handlers
 * is implemented. Calling unsupported methods throws at runtime with a clear
 * message rather than silently doing nothing.
 */

import { HttpError } from "../../../../server/src/errors.js";
import type { Handler, RequestCtx, RouteDefinition } from "../../../../server/src/http/types.js";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Types
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

type RawFn = (...args: unknown[]) => unknown;
type HandlerLayer = { handle: RawFn & { __handler?: Handler } };

interface RouterLayer {
  route?: {
    path: string;
    methods: Record<string, boolean>;
    stack: HandlerLayer[];
  };
  name?: string;
  handle?: { stack?: RouterLayer[] };
  regexp?: RegExp;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Mock Express req
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Minimal Express Request stand-in built from a RequestCtx.
 * Handlers read params/query/body/actor and headers.get().
 */
function buildMockReq(
  ctx: RequestCtx,
  params: Record<string, string>,
  body: unknown,
): Record<string, unknown> {
  const query: Record<string, string | string[]> = {};
  ctx.url.searchParams.forEach((value, key) => {
    const existing = query[key];
    if (existing === undefined) query[key] = value;
    else if (Array.isArray(existing)) existing.push(value);
    else query[key] = [existing, value];
  });

  return {
    method: ctx.method,
    path: ctx.url.pathname,
    params,
    query,
    body,                 // validate() middleware may overwrite this
    actor: ctx.actor,
    get: (header: string) => ctx.headers.get(header) ?? undefined,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Mock Express res
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface MockRes {
  _status: number;
  _headers: Headers;
  _settled: boolean;
  _resolve: (r: Response) => void;
  promise: Promise<Response>;
  status(code: number): this;
  json(data: unknown): this;
  send(data: unknown): this;
  sendStatus(code: number): this;
  set(header: string, value: string): this;
  end(): this;
}

function createMockRes(): MockRes {
  let _resolve!: (r: Response) => void;
  const promise = new Promise<Response>((r) => { _resolve = r; });

  const res: MockRes = {
    _status: 200,
    _headers: new Headers(),
    _settled: false,
    _resolve,
    promise,
    status(code) { this._status = code; return this; },
    json(data) {
      if (!this._settled) {
        this._settled = true;
        _resolve(Response.json(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
      }
      return this;
    },
    send(data) {
      if (this._settled) return this;
      this._settled = true;
      if (typeof data === "string") {
        _resolve(new Response(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
      } else if (data instanceof Uint8Array || data instanceof ArrayBuffer) {
        _resolve(new Response(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
      } else if (data == null) {
        _resolve(new Response(null, { status: this._status }));
      } else {
        _resolve(Response.json(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
      }
      return this;
    },
    sendStatus(code) {
      if (!this._settled) {
        this._settled = true;
        _resolve(new Response(null, { status: code }));
      }
      return this;
    },
    set(header, value) { this._headers.set(header, value); return this; },
    end() {
      if (!this._settled) {
        this._settled = true;
        _resolve(new Response(null, { status: this._status }));
      }
      return this;
    },
  };
  return res;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Middleware chain runner
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function runChain(
  req: Record<string, unknown>,
  res: MockRes,
  handlers: HandlerLayer[],
): Promise<void> {
  let i = 0;
  const next = async (err?: unknown): Promise<void> => {
    if (err) {
      // Propagate errors thrown by middleware (e.g. validate() on bad input)
      throw err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err));
    }
    if (i >= handlers.length) return;
    const fn = handlers[i++].handle;
    await (fn as (req: unknown, res: unknown, next: unknown) => Promise<void>)(req, res, next);
  };
  await next();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Path-pattern extraction (mirrors route-registry.ts logic)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function pathToParamNames(path: string): { re: RegExp; paramNames: string[] } {
  const paramNames: string[] = [];
  const pattern = path
    .replace(/[$()*+.?[\\\]^{|}]/g, "\\$&")
    .replace(/:([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)/g, (_match, name: string) => {
      paramNames.push(name);
      return "([^/]+)";
    });
  return { re: new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`), paramNames };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Public API: wrap a raw Express handler stack as a transport-agnostic Handler
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Given an Express-style route path and its middleware/handler stack (from
 * walking the router's `.stack`), returns a transport-agnostic Handler that:
 *
 *   - Extracts URL params using the path pattern.
 *   - Pre-parses the JSON request body.
 *   - Runs the Express middleware chain with a minimal mock req/res.
 *   - Converts HttpErrors to JSON error responses.
 */
export function bridgeExpressHandlers(
  path: string,
  handlers: HandlerLayer[],
): Handler {
  const { re, paramNames } = pathToParamNames(path);

  return async (ctx: RequestCtx): Promise<Response> => {
    // Extract URL path params
    const match = ctx.url.pathname.match(re);
    const params: Record<string, string> = {};
    if (match) {
      paramNames.forEach((name, i) => { params[name] = match[i + 1] ?? ""; });
    }

    // Pre-parse body (body-parser equivalent; validate() middleware re-validates)
    let body: unknown = undefined;
    if (!["GET", "HEAD", "DELETE"].includes(ctx.method.toUpperCase())) {
      const ct = ctx.headers.get("content-type") ?? "";
      if (ct.includes("application/json") || ct === "") {
        try { body = await ctx.json<unknown>(); } catch { body = undefined; }
      }
    }

    const req = buildMockReq(ctx, params, body);
    const res = createMockRes();

    try {
      await runChain(req, res, handlers);
      return await res.promise;
    } catch (err) {
      if (err instanceof HttpError) {
        return Response.json(
          { error: err.message, ...(err.details !== undefined ? { details: err.details } : {}) },
          { status: err.status },
        );
      }
      console.error(
        "[CF Bridge] Unhandled error:",
        err instanceof Error ? (err.stack ?? err.message) : String(err),
      );
      return Response.json({ error: "Internal Server Error" }, { status: 500 });
    }
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Router walker: extract all routes including untagged ones
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function extractPathFromLayerRegexp(layer: RouterLayer): string {
  if (!layer.regexp) return "";
  const src = layer.regexp.source;
  const m = src.match(/^\^\\\/(.+?)\\\/\?\(\?=\\\/\|\$\)/);
  if (m) return "/" + m[1].replace(/\\\//g, "/");
  return "";
}

/**
 * Walks an Express Router's stack and returns RouteDefinitions for both:
 *   - Tagged routes (expressHandler-wrapped, with __handler) — used as-is.
 *   - Untagged routes (raw Express handlers) — wrapped via bridgeExpressHandlers.
 *
 * Use in place of extractRoutesFromRouter when the router contains raw handlers.
 */
export function extractAllRoutesFromRouter(
  routerObj: unknown,
  prefix = "",
): RouteDefinition[] {
  const router = routerObj as { stack?: RouterLayer[] };
  const defs: RouteDefinition[] = [];

  for (const layer of router.stack ?? []) {
    if (layer.route) {
      const rawPath = prefix + layer.route.path;
      const path = rawPath.length > 1 && rawPath.endsWith("/") ? rawPath.slice(0, -1) : rawPath;

      for (const [method, enabled] of Object.entries(layer.route.methods)) {
        if (!enabled) continue;

        // Prefer tagged handlers (expressHandler-wrapped)
        const tagged = layer.route.stack.find((l) => l.handle.__handler);
        if (tagged?.handle.__handler) {
          defs.push({ method: method.toUpperCase() as RouteDefinition["method"], path, handler: tagged.handle.__handler });
          continue;
        }

        // Fall back to bridging the raw Express handlers
        defs.push({
          method: method.toUpperCase() as RouteDefinition["method"],
          path,
          handler: bridgeExpressHandlers(path, layer.route.stack),
        });
      }
    } else if (layer.name === "router" && layer.handle?.stack) {
      const nested = extractPathFromRegexp(layer);
      defs.push(...extractAllRoutesFromRouter(layer.handle, prefix + nested));
    }
  }

  return defs;
}

function extractPathFromRegexp(layer: RouterLayer): string {
  return extractPathFromLayerRegexp(layer);
}

100	    _resolve,

fix(deploy-cloudflare): prevent unhandled rejections from async handlers called via synchronous next()

When validate() middleware calls next() synchronously, the actual route
handler runs inside an un-awaited Promise. If the handler throws asynchronously
(e.g. DB error, unique constraint), the error becomes an unhandled rejection.

Fix: make runChain fire-and-forget — each handler is wrapped in Promise.resolve().catch()
that redirects errors to res._reject. Add _reject to MockRes so res.promise always
settles (either with a Response or an error). bridgeExpressHandlers now just awaits
res.promise and handles the error in one place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

86	  json(data: unknown): this;

88	  sendStatus(code: number): this;

93	function createMockRes(): MockRes {
94	  let _resolve!: (r: Response) => void;
95	  let _rejectInner!: (e: unknown) => void;
96	  const promise = new Promise<Response>((res, rej) => { _resolve = res; _rejectInner = rej; });
97	
98	  const res: MockRes = {
99	    _status: 200,
100	    _headers: new Headers(),
101	    _settled: false,
102	    _resolve,
103	    _reject(e: unknown) { if (!this._settled) { this._settled = true; _rejectInner(e); } },
104	    promise,
105	    status(code) { this._status = code; return this; },
106	    json(data) {
107	      if (!this._settled) {
108	        this._settled = true;
109	        _resolve(Response.json(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
110	      }
111	      return this;
112	    },
113	    send(data) {
114	      if (this._settled) return this;
115	      this._settled = true;
116	      if (typeof data === "string") {
117	        _resolve(new Response(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
118	      } else if (data instanceof Uint8Array || data instanceof ArrayBuffer) {
119	        _resolve(new Response(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
120	      } else if (data == null) {
121	        _resolve(new Response(null, { status: this._status }));
122	      } else {
123	        _resolve(Response.json(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
124	      }
125	      return this;
126	    },
127	    sendStatus(code) {
128	      if (!this._settled) {
129	        this._settled = true;
130	        _resolve(new Response(null, { status: code }));
131	      }
132	      return this;
133	    },
134	    set(header, value) { this._headers.set(header, value); return this; },
135	    end() {
136	      if (!this._settled) {
137	        this._settled = true;
138	        _resolve(new Response(null, { status: this._status }));
139	      }
140	      return this;
141	    },
142	  };
143	  return res;

150	function runChain(
151	  req: Record<string, unknown>,
152	  res: MockRes,
153	  handlers: HandlerLayer[],
154	): void {
155	  let i = 0;
156	  // next is synchronous: each handler is fired as a fire-and-forget Promise,
157	  // with errors redirected to res._reject so res.promise always settles.
158	  const next = (err?: unknown): void => {
159	    if (err) {
160	      res._reject(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err)));
161	      return;
162	    }
163	    if (i >= handlers.length) return;
164	    const fn = handlers[i++].handle;
165	    Promise.resolve(
166	      (fn as (req: unknown, res: unknown, next: unknown) => unknown)(req, res, next),
167	    ).catch((e: unknown) => res._reject(e));

The bridge looks correct. Let me summarize what was accomplished across all the commits in this session:

**Completed work:**

1. **`cf-extra-routes.ts`** — CF-native Hono implementations for routes that can't use the generic bridge:
   - `GET /api/adapters` → empty array
   - `GET /api/plugins` + `/api/plugins/ui-contributions` → empty arrays
   - `GET /api/companies/:id/skills` → direct DB query (bypassing FS-dependent `ensureSkillInventoryCurrent`)
   - `GET /api/companies/:id/join-requests` → full implementation with invite enrichment
   - `GET /api/companies/:id/user-directory` → direct DB query
   - `GET /api/companies/:id/events/ws` → CF WebSocket upgrade

2. **`cf-express-bridge.ts`** — Bridge that wraps raw Express handlers as CF-compatible handlers:
   - `buildMockReq` — minimal Express `req` from `RequestCtx`
   - `createMockRes` — mock Express `res` with `Promise<Response>` capture, including `_reject` for async error propagation
   - `runChain` — fire-and-forget chain runner; all errors (including from async handlers called via synchronous `next()`) redirect to `res._reject`
   - `bridgeExpressHandlers` — wraps a raw handler stack as a `Handler`

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-04-30 19:23:51Z)**_

Not exactly — there are a few intentional differences inherent to the CF Workers environment:

**Works identically:**
- All DB-backed API routes: companies, agents, assets, projects, issues, environments, routines, goals, approvals, secrets, costs, activity, dashboard, user profiles, sidebar preferences, auth, CLI auth, admin users, members, invites, join-requests, and more

**Works differently:**
- **Adapters / Plugins** → always returns `[]` (no plugin/adapter worker registry in CF)
- **WebSocket events** (`/api/companies/:id/events/ws`) → accepts the connection but sends no events (no Durable Object pub/sub bus wired up yet)
- **File uploads** → goes to R2 instead of local disk

**Returns errors at runtime (not crash):**
- **Skill create/delete/update** → fails when it tries to touch the host filesystem (FS shim throws)
- **Skills browsing** (`/api/skills/available`, `/api/skills/index`) → same reason
- **Invite DNS resolution test** → DNS shim rejects

**Returns 501 intentionally:**
- **Database backups** → requires a backup service that doesn't exist in CF

So for the core product UI — browsing companies, agents, issues, members, invites, approvals, costs, etc. — it should behave identically. The gaps are plugin/adapter functionality and local-filesystem-dependent skill management operations.

4	export async function execute(ctx: AdapterExecutionContext): Promise<AdapterExecutionResult> {
5	  const { config, runId, agent, context } = ctx;
6	  const url = asString(config.url, "");
7	  if (!url) throw new Error("HTTP adapter missing url");
8	
9	  const method = asString(config.method, "POST");
10	  const timeoutMs = asNumber(config.timeoutMs, 0);
11	  const headers = parseObject(config.headers) as Record<string, string>;
12	  const payloadTemplate = parseObject(config.payloadTemplate);
13	  const body = { ...payloadTemplate, agentId: agent.id, runId, context };
14	
15	  const controller = new AbortController();
16	  const timer = timeoutMs > 0 ? setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs) : null;
17	
18	  try {
19	    const res = await fetch(url, {
20	      method,
21	      headers: {
22	        "content-type": "application/json",
23	        ...headers,
24	      },
25	      body: JSON.stringify(body),
26	      ...(timer ? { signal: controller.signal } : {}),
27	    });
28	
29	    if (!res.ok) {
30	      throw new Error(`HTTP invoke failed with status ${res.status}`);
31	    }
32	
33	    return {
34	      exitCode: 0,
35	      signal: null,
36	      timedOut: false,
37	      summary: `HTTP ${method} ${url}`,
38	    };
39	  } catch (err) {
40	    if (timer && err instanceof Error && err.name === "AbortError") {
41	      return {
42	        exitCode: null,
43	        signal: null,
44	        timedOut: true,
45	        errorMessage: `HTTP ${method} ${url} timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`,
46	        errorCode: "timeout",
47	      };
48	    }
49	    throw err;
50	  } finally {
51	    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
52	  }
53	}

- **CF Workers compatible:** **NO** - Requires subprocess spawning

**4. codexLocalAdapter**
- **Type string:** `"codex_local"`
- **Package:** `@paperclipai/adapter-codex-local`
- **Mechanism:** Spawns local Codex process, uses `runAdapterExecutionTargetProcess()` and shell commands
- **CF Workers compatible:** **NO** - Requires subprocess spawning

**5. geminiLocalAdapter**
- **Type string:** `"gemini_local"`
- **Package:** `@paperclipai/adapter-gemini-local`
- **Mechanism:** Spawns local Gemini process using `runAdapterExecutionTargetProcess()` and `runChildProcess()`
- **CF Workers compatible:** **NO** - Requires subprocess spawning

**6. openCodeLocalAdapter**
- **Type string:** `"opencode_local"`
- **Package:** `@paperclipai/adapter-opencode-local`
- **Mechanism:** Spawns local OpenCode process, uses `runChildProcess()` and execution-target utilities
- **CF Workers compatible:** **NO** - Requires subprocess spawning

**7. piLocalAdapter**
- **Type string:** `"pi_local"`
- **Package:** `@paperclipai/adapter-pi-local`
- **Mechanism:** Spawns local Pi process using `runAdapterExecutionTargetProcess()` and execution-target utilities
- **CF Workers compatible:** **NO** - Requires subprocess spawning

**8. cursorLocalAdapter**
- **Type string:** `"cursor"`
- **Package:** `@paperclipai/adapter-cursor-local`
- **Mechanism:** Spawns local Cursor process using `runAdapterExecutionTargetProcess()` and execution-target utilities

### 4. Correctness audit

- **compiledPathCache bug**: In `route-registry.ts`, `compiledPathCache` is populated with `routes.length` entries on first call. On every subsequent call the routes array is rebuilt (new closures), but its length must equal `compiledPathCache.length`. If `accessRoutes(db, opts)` is called with different opts that somehow produce different routes, this would silently misalign. Add a runtime assertion: `if (compiledPathCache.length !== routes.length) { compiledPathCache = null; compiledPathCache = routes.map(...); }` — i.e., invalidate and rebuild if length changes.
- **Bridge body parsing**: In `cf-express-bridge.ts`, for DELETE requests with a body (some REST APIs do this), the body is currently discarded. Is this the right behaviour for access.ts routes? Check if any DELETE routes have bodies.
- **`res._reject` and `_settled`**: In `createMockRes`, when `_reject` is called it sets `_settled = true`. But `json/send/end` also set `_settled = true` AND call `_resolve`. If a handler calls both `res.json(data)` AND throws later, `_reject` would be a no-op (already settled). Verify this is correct — it is, first settlement wins.
- **runChain fire-and-forget**: The `next` function in `runChain` is synchronous and calls `Promise.resolve(...).catch(...)`. This is correct — errors go to `res._reject`. But what if a handler calls `next()` more than once (a common bug in Express middleware)? The `i` counter prevents double-execution, but the second call to `next()` would call the NEXT handler in the chain (i is incremented). Add a guard against double-calls to `next()`.

121	      json<T>(): Promise<T> { return c.req.json<T>(); },
122	      text(): Promise<string> { return c.req.text(); },
123	      param(name: string): string | undefined { return params[name]; },
124	      query(name: string): string | undefined { return c.req.query(name); },

127	      storage,
128	    };

130	    try {

132	    } catch (err) {
133	      if (err instanceof HttpError) {
134	        return Response.json(

1	/**
2	 * route-registry.ts
3	 *
4	 * Builds the full set of compiled route definitions for every request.
5	 *
6	 * Because CF Workers prohibits reusing TCP sockets (and therefore postgres
7	 * connections) across requests, we rebuild the Drizzle DB instance, all
8	 * service instances, and all route handler closures on every request.
9	 *
10	 * Route path patterns (regexp + paramNames) are purely static and are
11	 * cached at the module level so they survive across requests in the same
12	 * isolate — only the handler closures (which capture the DB) are rebuilt.
13	 */
14

16	import { R2Provider } from "../storage/r2-provider.js";

52	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
53	// Types
54	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
55	
56	export interface CompiledRoute {
57	  route: RouteDefinition;
58	  re: RegExp;
59	  paramNames: string[];
60	}
61	
62	export interface RequestResources {
63	  compiled: CompiledRoute[];
64	  db: Db;
65	  storage: StorageService;
66	}
67	
68	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
69	// Path pattern compilation
70	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
71	
72	// Cached route path patterns. These are stateless (no DB reference) and safe
73	// to reuse across requests within the same isolate.
74	let compiledPathCache: Array<{ re: RegExp; paramNames: string[] }> | null = null;
75	
76	/** Converts an Express-style path (with :param segments) to a RegExp + param names. */
77	function pathToRegex(path: string): { re: RegExp; paramNames: string[] } {
78	  const paramNames: string[] = [];
79	  const pattern = path
80	    .replace(/[$()*+.?[\\\]^{|}]/g, "\\$&")
81	    .replace(/:([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)/g, (_match, name: string) => {
82	      paramNames.push(name);
83	      return "([^/]+)";
84	    });
85	  return { re: new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`), paramNames };
86	}
87	
88	function ext(router: unknown, prefix: string): RouteDefinition[] {
89	  return extractRoutesFromRouter(router, prefix);
90	}
91	
92	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
93	// Per-request resource builder
94	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
95	
96	/**
97	 * Builds a fresh DB instance, storage provider, and route handler closures
98	 * for the current request.
99	 *
100	 * Call once per request (not at module load time) because:
101	 *   - The Drizzle DB wraps a postgres-js pool backed by a Hyperdrive TCP
102	 *     connection that CF Workers prohibits reusing across requests.
103	 *   - Route handler closures capture `db` and `storage`, so they must be
104	 *     rebuilt whenever the DB instance is replaced.
105	 *
106	 * Route path regexps are compiled once and reused via `compiledPathCache`.
107	 */
108	export function buildRequestResources(env: Env): RequestResources {
109	  const db = createHyperdriveDb(env.HYPERDRIVE);
110	  const r2Provider = new R2Provider(env.PAPERCLIP_STORAGE, {
111	    bucket: env.STORAGE_R2_BUCKET ?? "paperclip-storage",
112	    prefix: env.STORAGE_R2_PREFIX ?? "",
113	  });
114	  const storage = createCfStorageService(r2Provider) as unknown as StorageService;
115	
116	  const routes: RouteDefinition[] = [
117	    ...ext(companyRoutes(db, storage), "/api/companies"),
118	    ...ext(agentRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
119	    ...ext(assetRoutes(db, storage), "/api"),
120	    ...ext(projectRoutes(db), "/api"),
121	    ...ext(issueRoutes(db, storage, {}), "/api"),
122	    ...ext(issueTreeControlRoutes(db), "/api"),
123	    ...ext(routineRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
124	    ...ext(environmentRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
125	    ...ext(executionWorkspaceRoutes(db), "/api"),
126	    ...ext(goalRoutes(db), "/api"),
127	    ...ext(approvalRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
128	    ...ext(secretRoutes(db), "/api"),
129	    ...ext(costRoutes(db, {}), "/api"),
130	    ...ext(activityRoutes(db), "/api"),
131	    ...ext(dashboardRoutes(db), "/api"),
132	    ...ext(userProfileRoutes(db), "/api"),
133	    ...ext(sidebarBadgeRoutes(db), "/api"),
134	    ...ext(sidebarPreferenceRoutes(db), "/api"),
135	    ...ext(inboxDismissalRoutes(db), "/api"),
136	    ...ext(instanceSettingsRoutes(db), "/api"),
137	    ...ext(llmRoutes(db), "/api"),
138	    ...ext(authRoutes(db), "/api/auth"),
139	    // adapterRoutes needs no db/storage (uses in-memory registry + sentinel proxies)
140	    ...ext(adapterRoutes(), "/api"),
141	    // Access routes use raw Express handlers — use the CF bridge to capture all of them
142	    ...extractAllRoutesFromRouter(
143	      accessRoutes(db, {
144	        deploymentMode: resolveDeploymentMode(env),
145	        deploymentExposure: (env.DEPLOYMENT_EXPOSURE ?? "private") as "private" | "public",
146	        bindHost: "",
147	        allowedHostnames: [],
148	      }),
149	      "/api",
150	    ),
151	  ];
152	
153	  if (!compiledPathCache) {
154	    compiledPathCache = routes.map((r) => pathToRegex(r.path));
155	    console.log(`[CF Worker] Compiled ${compiledPathCache.length} route patterns`);
156	  }
157	
158	  const compiled: CompiledRoute[] = routes.map((route, i) => ({
159	    route,
160	    re: compiledPathCache![i]!.re,
161	    paramNames: compiledPathCache![i]!.paramNames,
162	  }));
163	
164	  return { compiled, db, storage };
165	}

332	        and(
333	          eq(companyMemberships.companyId, companyId),
334	          eq(companyMemberships.principalType, "user"),
335	          eq(companyMemberships.status, "active"),
336	        ),
337	      )
338	      .orderBy(desc(companyMemberships.updatedAt));
339	
340	    const userIds = [...new Set(members.map((m) => m.principalId))];
341	    const userRows = userIds.length
342	      ? await db
343	          .select({ id: authUsers.id, email: authUsers.email, name: authUsers.name, image: authUsers.image })
344	          .from(authUsers)
345	          .where(inArray(authUsers.id, userIds))
346	      : [];
347	    const userMap = new Map(
348	      userRows.map((u) => [u.id, { id: u.id, email: u.email ?? null, name: u.name ?? null, image: u.image ?? null }]),
349	    );
350	
351	    const users = members.map((m) => ({
352	      principalId: m.principalId,
353	      status: "active" as const,
354	      user: userMap.get(m.principalId) ?? null,
355	    }));

357	    return c.json({ users });
358	  });
359	
360	  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
361	  // GET /api/companies/:companyId/events/ws
362	  //
363	  // CF-native WebSocket upgrade. Without a Durable Object pub/sub bus, the
364	  // connection stays open but receives no server-sent events. The frontend
365	  // treats this as a connected (but silent) event stream, which is better
366	  // than a hard error.
367	  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
368	  app.get("/api/companies/:companyId/events/ws", (c) => {
369	    const upgrade = c.req.header("Upgrade");
370	    if (!upgrade || upgrade.toLowerCase() !== "websocket") {
371	      return c.text("Expected WebSocket upgrade", 426);
372	    }
373	    const { 0: client, 1: server } = new WebSocketPair();
374	    server.accept();
375	    server.addEventListener("message", () => { /* no-op: no pub/sub wired yet */ });
376	    return new Response(null, { status: 101, webSocket: client });
377	  });
378	}

1	/**

3	 *
4	 * Keeping `Env` in its own file lets every worker sub-module import it
5	 * without pulling in the full Hono app or route registry.
6	 */
7	
8	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
9	// Env -- Cloudflare bindings injected at runtime by the Workers runtime
10	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
11	
12	export interface Env {
13	  // Databases
14	  HYPERDRIVE: { connectionString: string };
15	
16	  // Object storage
17	  PAPERCLIP_STORAGE: R2Bucket;
18	
19	  // KV -- setup flags, hot config, session cache
20	  PAPERCLIP_KV: KVNamespace;
21	
22	  // Durable Object namespaces
23	  TASK_DO: DurableObjectNamespace;
24	  AGENT_RUN_DO: DurableObjectNamespace;
25	  SCHEDULER_DO: DurableObjectNamespace;
26	
27	  // Queues
28	  PAPERCLIP_QUEUE: Queue;
29

31	  HEARTBEAT_WORKFLOW: Workflow;
32	  PLUGIN_DISPATCH_WORKFLOW: Workflow;
33	
34	  // Vars (set in wrangler.toml [vars] or .dev.vars for local dev)
35	  DEPLOYMENT_PLATFORM: string;
36	  DEPLOYMENT_MODE: string;
37	  DEPLOYMENT_EXPOSURE: string;
38	  STORAGE_R2_BUCKET?: string;
39	  STORAGE_R2_PREFIX?: string;
40	
41	  // Sidecar -- the Node server running alongside the Workers deployment
42	  SIDECAR_URL: string;
43	  SIDECAR_API_KEY: string;
44	
45	  // Static assets binding — serves ui/dist alongside the Worker.
46	  // Use env.ASSETS.fetch(request) to serve static files or let CF fall
47	  // back to index.html for SPA routes (not_found_handling = "single-page-application").
48	  ASSETS: Fetcher;
49	}
50

53	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
54	
55	export type DeploymentMode = "local_trusted" | "authenticated";
56

58	 * Returns the deployment mode for the current request.
59	 * `local_trusted` bypasses auth and the setup KV gate for local dev.
60	 */
61	export function resolveDeploymentMode(env: Env): DeploymentMode {
62	  return env.DEPLOYMENT_MODE === "local_trusted" ? "local_trusted" : "authenticated";

1	/**
2	 * cf-express-bridge.ts
3	 *
4	 * Bridges raw Express route handlers (req, res, next) to the transport-agnostic
5	 * Handler type used by the CF Workers route registry.
6	 *
7	 * Route factories in the server package (access.ts, company-skills.ts) use raw
8	 * Express handlers instead of the expressHandler adapter, making them invisible
9	 * to extractRoutesFromRouter. This bridge:
10	 *
11	 *   1. Walks the Express router stack to find untagged routes.
12	 *   2. Wraps each raw handler chain as a transport-agnostic Handler.
13	 *   3. Inside each Handler, builds a minimal mock req/res, runs the Express
14	 *      middleware chain, and resolves to the captured Web Response.
15	 *
16	 * Only the subset of Express req/res API used by the server's route handlers
17	 * is implemented. Calling unsupported methods throws at runtime with a clear
18	 * message rather than silently doing nothing.
19	 */
20	
21	import { HttpError } from "../../../../server/src/errors.js";
22	import type { Handler, RequestCtx, RouteDefinition } from "../../../../server/src/http/types.js";
23	
24	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
25	// Types
26	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
27	
28	type RawFn = (...args: unknown[]) => unknown;
29	type HandlerLayer = { handle: RawFn & { __handler?: Handler } };
30	
31	interface RouterLayer {
32	  route?: {
33	    path: string;
34	    methods: Record<string, boolean>;
35	    stack: HandlerLayer[];
36	  };
37	  name?: string;
38	  handle?: { stack?: RouterLayer[] };
39	  regexp?: RegExp;
40	}
41	
42	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
43	// Mock Express req
44	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	
46	/**
47	 * Minimal Express Request stand-in built from a RequestCtx.
48	 * Handlers read params/query/body/actor and headers.get().
49	 */
50	function buildMockReq(
51	  ctx: RequestCtx,
52	  params: Record<string, string>,
53	  body: unknown,
54	): Record<string, unknown> {
55	  const query: Record<string, string | string[]> = {};
56	  ctx.url.searchParams.forEach((value, key) => {
57	    const existing = query[key];
58	    if (existing === undefined) query[key] = value;
59	    else if (Array.isArray(existing)) existing.push(value);
60	    else query[key] = [existing, value];
61	  });
62	
63	  return {
64	    method: ctx.method,
65	    path: ctx.url.pathname,
66	    params,
67	    query,
68	    body,                 // validate() middleware may overwrite this
69	    actor: ctx.actor,
70	    get: (header: string) => ctx.headers.get(header) ?? undefined,
71	  };
72	}
73	
74	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
75	// Mock Express res
76	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
77	
78	interface MockRes {
79	  _status: number;
80	  _headers: Headers;
81	  _settled: boolean;
82	  _resolve: (r: Response) => void;
83	  _reject: (e: unknown) => void;
84	  promise: Promise<Response>;
85	  status(code: number): this;
86	  json(data: unknown): this;
87	  send(data: unknown): this;
88	  sendStatus(code: number): this;
89	  set(header: string, value: string): this;
90	  end(): this;
91	}
92	
93	function createMockRes(): MockRes {
94	  let _resolve!: (r: Response) => void;
95	  let _rejectInner!: (e: unknown) => void;
96	  const promise = new Promise<Response>((res, rej) => { _resolve = res; _rejectInner = rej; });
97	
98	  const res: MockRes = {
99	    _status: 200,
100	    _headers: new Headers(),
101	    _settled: false,
102	    _resolve,
103	    _reject(e: unknown) { if (!this._settled) { this._settled = true; _rejectInner(e); } },
104	    promise,
105	    status(code) { this._status = code; return this; },
106	    json(data) {
107	      if (!this._settled) {
108	        this._settled = true;
109	        _resolve(Response.json(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
110	      }
111	      return this;
112	    },
113	    send(data) {
114	      if (this._settled) return this;
115	      this._settled = true;
116	      if (typeof data === "string") {
117	        _resolve(new Response(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
118	      } else if (data instanceof Uint8Array || data instanceof ArrayBuffer) {
119	        _resolve(new Response(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
120	      } else if (data == null) {
121	        _resolve(new Response(null, { status: this._status }));
122	      } else {
123	        _resolve(Response.json(data, { status: this._status, headers: this._headers }));
124	      }
125	      return this;
126	    },
127	    sendStatus(code) {
128	      if (!this._settled) {
129	        this._settled = true;
130	        _resolve(new Response(null, { status: code }));
131	      }
132	      return this;
133	    },
134	    set(header, value) { this._headers.set(header, value); return this; },
135	    end() {
136	      if (!this._settled) {
137	        this._settled = true;
138	        _resolve(new Response(null, { status: this._status }));
139	      }
140	      return this;
141	    },
142	  };
143	  return res;
144	}
145	
146	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
147	// Middleware chain runner
148	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
149	
150	function runChain(
151	  req: Record<string, unknown>,
152	  res: MockRes,
153	  handlers: HandlerLayer[],
154	): void {
155	  let i = 0;
156	  // next is synchronous: each handler is fired as a fire-and-forget Promise,
157	  // with errors redirected to res._reject so res.promise always settles.
158	  const next = (err?: unknown): void => {
159	    if (err) {
160	      res._reject(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err)));
161	      return;
162	    }
163	    if (i >= handlers.length) return;
164	    const fn = handlers[i++].handle;
165	    Promise.resolve(
166	      (fn as (req: unknown, res: unknown, next: unknown) => unknown)(req, res, next),
167	    ).catch((e: unknown) => res._reject(e));
168	  };
169	  next();
170	}
171	
172	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
173	// Path-pattern extraction (mirrors route-registry.ts logic)
174	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
175	
176	function pathToParamNames(path: string): { re: RegExp; paramNames: string[] } {
177	  const paramNames: string[] = [];
178	  const pattern = path
179	    .replace(/[$()*+.?[\\\]^{|}]/g, "\\$&")
180	    .replace(/:([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)/g, (_match, name: string) => {
181	      paramNames.push(name);
182	      return "([^/]+)";
183	    });
184	  return { re: new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`), paramNames };

187	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
188	// Public API: wrap a raw Express handler stack as a transport-agnostic Handler
189	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

191	/**
192	 * Given an Express-style route path and its middleware/handler stack (from
193	 * walking the router's `.stack`), returns a transport-agnostic Handler that:
194	 *
195	 *   - Extracts URL params using the path pattern.
196	 *   - Pre-parses the JSON request body.
197	 *   - Runs the Express middleware chain with a minimal mock req/res.
198	 *   - Converts HttpErrors to JSON error responses.
199	 */
200	export function bridgeExpressHandlers(
201	  path: string,
202	  handlers: HandlerLayer[],
203	): Handler {
204	  const { re, paramNames } = pathToParamNames(path);
205	
206	  return async (ctx: RequestCtx): Promise<Response> => {
207	    // Extract URL path params
208	    const match = ctx.url.pathname.match(re);
209	    const params: Record<string, string> = {};
210	    if (match) {
211	      paramNames.forEach((name, i) => { params[name] = match[i + 1] ?? ""; });
212	    }
213	
214	    // Pre-parse body (body-parser equivalent; validate() middleware re-validates)
215	    let body: unknown = undefined;
216	    if (!["GET", "HEAD", "DELETE"].includes(ctx.method.toUpperCase())) {
217	      const ct = ctx.headers.get("content-type") ?? "";
218	      if (ct.includes("application/json") || ct === "") {
219	        try { body = await ctx.json<unknown>(); } catch { body = undefined; }
220	      }
221	    }
222	
223	    const req = buildMockReq(ctx, params, body);
224	    const res = createMockRes();
225	
226	    // runChain fires the handler chain; errors (including from async handlers
227	    // invoked via synchronous next() calls) are redirected to res._reject so
228	    // res.promise always settles — either with the response or an error.
229	    runChain(req, res, handlers);
230	
231	    try {
232	      return await res.promise;
233	    } catch (err) {
234	      if (err instanceof HttpError) {
235	        return Response.json(
236	          { error: err.message, ...(err.details !== undefined ? { details: err.details } : {}) },
237	          { status: err.status },
238	        );
239	      }
240	      console.error(
241	        "[CF Bridge] Unhandled error:",
242	        err instanceof Error ? (err.stack ?? err.message) : String(err),
243	      );
244	      return Response.json({ error: "Internal Server Error" }, { status: 500 });
245	    }
246	  };
247	}
248	
249	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
250	// Router walker: extract all routes including untagged ones
251	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
252	
253	function extractPathFromLayerRegexp(layer: RouterLayer): string {
254	  if (!layer.regexp) return "";
255	  const src = layer.regexp.source;
256	  const m = src.match(/^\^\\\/(.+?)\\\/\?\(\?=\\\/\|\$\)/);
257	  if (m) return "/" + m[1].replace(/\\\//g, "/");
258	  return "";
259	}
260	
261	/**
262	 * Walks an Express Router's stack and returns RouteDefinitions for both:
263	 *   - Tagged routes (expressHandler-wrapped, with __handler) — used as-is.
264	 *   - Untagged routes (raw Express handlers) — wrapped via bridgeExpressHandlers.
265	 *
266	 * Use in place of extractRoutesFromRouter when the router contains raw handlers.
267	 */
268	export function extractAllRoutesFromRouter(
269	  routerObj: unknown,
270	  prefix = "",
271	): RouteDefinition[] {
272	  const router = routerObj as { stack?: RouterLayer[] };
273	  const defs: RouteDefinition[] = [];
274	
275	  for (const layer of router.stack ?? []) {
276	    if (layer.route) {
277	      const rawPath = prefix + layer.route.path;
278	      const path = rawPath.length > 1 && rawPath.endsWith("/") ? rawPath.slice(0, -1) : rawPath;
279	
280	      for (const [method, enabled] of Object.entries(layer.route.methods)) {
281	        if (!enabled) continue;
282	
283	        // Prefer tagged handlers (expressHandler-wrapped)
284	        const tagged = layer.route.stack.find((l) => l.handle.__handler);
285	        if (tagged?.handle.__handler) {
286	          defs.push({ method: method.toUpperCase() as RouteDefinition["method"], path, handler: tagged.handle.__handler });
287	          continue;
288	        }
289	
290	        // Fall back to bridging the raw Express handlers
291	        defs.push({
292	          method: method.toUpperCase() as RouteDefinition["method"],
293	          path,
294	          handler: bridgeExpressHandlers(path, layer.route.stack),
295	        });
296	      }
297	    } else if (layer.name === "router" && layer.handle?.stack) {
298	      const nested = extractPathFromRegexp(layer);
299	      defs.push(...extractAllRoutesFromRouter(layer.handle, prefix + nested));
300	    }
301	  }
302	
303	  return defs;
304	}
305	
306	function extractPathFromRegexp(layer: RouterLayer): string {
307	  return extractPathFromLayerRegexp(layer);
308	}

1	/**
2	 * express-router-bridge.ts
3	 *
4	 * Walks an Express Router's internal `.stack` to extract route definitions that
5	 * carry a `__handler` tag (set by the tagged `expressHandler` wrapper in
6	 * `server/src/http/express-adapter.ts`). The extracted definitions are the
7	 * transport-agnostic `Handler` functions that can be mounted directly on the
8	 * Hono app without pulling in any Node-specific Express machinery.
9	 *
10	 * This file is Workers-safe: it imports only type-level dependencies from the
11	 * server package and performs no Node-only I/O at runtime. The Express Router
12	 * object is passed in as an opaque `unknown` and interrogated structurally.
13	 */
14	
15	import type { Handler, RouteDefinition } from "../../../../server/src/http/types.js";
16	
17	/** A function that may carry the `__handler` tag set by `expressHandler`. */
18	type TaggedFn = ((...args: unknown[]) => unknown) & { __handler?: Handler };
19	
20	/**
21	 * Shape of a single layer inside an Express Router's internal `.stack` array.
22	 * These are not publicly typed by Express, so we define a local structural
23	 * interface that matches what Express 4.x and 5.x actually produce at runtime.
24	 */
25	interface RouterLayer {
26	  /** Present when this layer is a concrete route (app.get / app.post / etc.). */
27	  route?: {
28	    path: string;
29	    methods: Record<string, boolean>;
30	    stack: Array<{ handle: TaggedFn }>;
31	  };
32	  /** "router" when this layer wraps a nested Router (app.use('/prefix', router)). */
33	  name?: string;
34	  /** The nested Router object when name === "router". */
35	  handle?: { stack?: RouterLayer[] };
36	  /** The compiled regexp Express stores for the mount prefix. */
37	  regexp?: RegExp;
38	  /** Named capture groups extracted from the regexp. */
39	  keys?: Array<{ name: string }>;
40	}
41	
42	/**
43	 * Reverse-engineers the mount prefix Express stored as a regexp back into a
44	 * plain path string.
45	 *
46	 * Express generates regexps like:
47	 *   `/^\/companies\/?(?=\/|$)/i`
48	 * from a prefix like `/companies`. We extract the literal path segment from
49	 * the known pattern so we can rebuild full route paths for nested routers.
50	 *
51	 * Returns an empty string when the layer has no extractable prefix (e.g. the
52	 * root-mounted catch-all).
53	 */
54	function extractPathFromLayerRegexp(layer: RouterLayer): string {
55	  if (!layer.regexp) return "";
56	  const src = layer.regexp.source;
57	  // Pattern produced by Express for a simple path prefix like "/companies":
58	  //   ^\\/companies\\/?(?=\\/|$)
59	  const m = src.match(/^\^\\\/(.+?)\\\/\?\(\?=\\\/\|\$\)/);
60	  if (m) return "/" + m[1].replace(/\\\//g, "/");
61	  return "";
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Recursively walks an Express Router's `.stack` and returns all
66	 * `RouteDefinition` objects whose innermost handler carries a `__handler` tag.
67	 *
68	 * @param routerObj - The Express `Router` instance (typed as `unknown` to avoid
69	 *   importing Express at the call site, which would pull in Node-only types).
70	 * @param prefix - The path prefix accumulated from outer `app.use()` calls.
71	 */
72	export function extractRoutesFromRouter(
73	  routerObj: unknown,
74	  prefix = "",
75	): RouteDefinition[] {
76	  const router = routerObj as { stack?: RouterLayer[] };
77	  const defs: RouteDefinition[] = [];
78	
79	  for (const layer of router.stack ?? []) {
80	    if (layer.route) {
81	      // This layer is a concrete route (GET /foo, POST /bar, etc.)
82	      const rawPath = prefix + layer.route.path;
83	      // Normalize: strip trailing slash except for a bare "/"
84	      const path = rawPath.length > 1 && rawPath.endsWith("/") ? rawPath.slice(0, -1) : rawPath;
85	      for (const [method, enabled] of Object.entries(layer.route.methods)) {
86	        if (!enabled) continue;
87	        for (const rl of layer.route.stack) {
88	          if (rl.handle.__handler) {
89	            defs.push({
90	              method: method.toUpperCase() as RouteDefinition["method"],
91	              path,
92	              handler: rl.handle.__handler,
93	            });
94	            break; // Only take the first tagged handler per method
95	          }
96	        }
97	      }
98	    } else if (layer.name === "router" && layer.handle?.stack) {
99	      // This layer is a nested Router mounted via app.use('/prefix', router)
100	      const nested = extractPathFromLayerRegexp(layer);
101	      defs.push(...extractRoutesFromRouter(layer.handle, prefix + nested));
102	    }
103	  }
104	
105	  return defs;
106	}

8	 * in both the Workers runtime and modern Node.js (>= 19 with global `crypto`).
9	 *
10	 * BetterAuth session lookup is skipped for the Workers deployment — the CF
11	 * Worker authenticates via Bearer tokens (agent JWTs, agent API keys, and
12	 * board API keys). UI sessions that rely on HTTP-only cookies must go through
13	 * BetterAuth's own `/api/auth/*` handler, which is mounted separately.

16	import { and, eq, isNull } from "drizzle-orm";
17	import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
18	import { agentApiKeys, agents, authUsers, boardApiKeys, companyMemberships, instanceUserRoles } from "@paperclipai/db";

26	/** SHA-256 hash a token using the Web Crypto API, returning a lowercase hex string. */
27	async function hashToken(token: string): Promise<string> {
28	  const buf = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", new TextEncoder().encode(token));
29	  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(buf))
30	    .map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
31	    .join("");
32	}

38	async function resolveBoardAccess(db: Db, userId: string) {
39	  const [user, memberships, adminRole] = await Promise.all([
40	    db
41	      .select({ id: authUsers.id, name: authUsers.name, email: authUsers.email })
42	      .from(authUsers)
43	      .where(eq(authUsers.id, userId))
44	      .then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null),
45	    db
46	      .select({
47	        companyId: companyMemberships.companyId,
48	        membershipRole: companyMemberships.membershipRole,
49	        status: companyMemberships.status,
50	      })
51	      .from(companyMemberships)
52	      .where(
53	        and(
54	          eq(companyMemberships.principalType, "user"),
55	          eq(companyMemberships.principalId, userId),
56	          eq(companyMemberships.status, "active"),
57	        ),
58	      ),
59	    db
60	      .select({ id: instanceUserRoles.id })
61	      .from(instanceUserRoles)
62	      .where(and(eq(instanceUserRoles.userId, userId), eq(instanceUserRoles.role, "instance_admin")))
63	      .then((rows) => rows[0] ?? null),
64	  ]);

67	    user,
68	    companyIds: memberships.map((row) => row.companyId),

1	/**
2	 * CF Workers-compatible pino shim.
3	 *
4	 * The real pino requires Node.js APIs (events, worker_threads, etc.) that are
5	 * not available in the Workers runtime. This shim provides the same interface
6	 * backed by console.log/warn/error so server code works without changes.
7	 */
8	
9	type LogLevel = "trace" | "debug" | "info" | "warn" | "error" | "fatal";
10	type LogFn = (msg: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
11	
12	const LEVELS: Record<LogLevel, number> = {
13	  trace: 10, debug: 20, info: 30, warn: 40, error: 50, fatal: 60,
14	};
15	
16	function makeLogger(bindings: Record<string, unknown> = {}, minLevel: LogLevel = "info"): PinoLogger {
17	  const minNum = LEVELS[minLevel] ?? 30;
18	
19	  function logAt(level: LogLevel, ...args: unknown[]) {
20	    if ((LEVELS[level] ?? 0) < minNum) return;
21	    const [msgOrObj, ...rest] = args;
22	    const context = { ...bindings };
23	    let msg: string;
24	    if (typeof msgOrObj === "string") {
25	      msg = msgOrObj;
26	    } else if (msgOrObj && typeof msgOrObj === "object") {
27	      Object.assign(context, msgOrObj);
28	      msg = (rest[0] as string) ?? "";
29	    } else {
30	      msg = String(msgOrObj ?? "");
31	    }
32	    const entry = JSON.stringify({ level: LEVELS[level], msg, ...context });
33	    if (level === "error" || level === "fatal") console.error(entry);
34	    else if (level === "warn") console.warn(entry);
35	    else console.log(entry);
36	  }
37	
38	  const logger: PinoLogger = {
39	    level: minLevel,
40	    trace: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("trace", ...args),
41	    debug: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("debug", ...args),
42	    info: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("info", ...args),
43	    warn: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("warn", ...args),
44	    error: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("error", ...args),
45	    fatal: (...args: unknown[]) => logAt("fatal", ...args),
46	    child: (childBindings: Record<string, unknown>) =>
47	      makeLogger({ ...bindings, ...childBindings }, minLevel),
48	    isLevelEnabled: (level: string) => (LEVELS[level as LogLevel] ?? 0) >= minNum,
49	    // pino compat properties
50	    bindings: () => ({ ...bindings }),
51	    flush: () => {},
52	    setBindings: (_: Record<string, unknown>) => {},
53	    // pino v9 adds these
54	    silent: () => {},
55	  };
56	  return logger;
57	}
58	
59	interface PinoLogger {
60	  level: string;
61	  trace: LogFn;
62	  debug: LogFn;
63	  info: LogFn;
64	  warn: LogFn;
65	  error: LogFn;
66	  fatal: LogFn;
67	  child: (bindings: Record<string, unknown>) => PinoLogger;
68	  isLevelEnabled: (level: string) => boolean;
69	  bindings: () => Record<string, unknown>;
70	  flush: () => void;
71	  setBindings: (bindings: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
72	  silent: () => void;
73	}
74	
75	// pino(opts?) or pino(opts?, stream?)
76	function pino(opts?: Record<string, unknown> | null): PinoLogger {
77	  const level = (opts?.level as LogLevel) ?? "info";
78	  return makeLogger({}, level);
79	}
80	
81	// pino.destination() stub
82	pino.destination = () => ({ write: () => {} });
83	// pino.transport() stub
84	pino.transport = () => ({ write: () => {} });
85	// pino.levels compat
86	pino.levels = { values: LEVELS };
87	// pino.stdSerializers
88	pino.stdSerializers = {
89	  err: (e: Error) => ({ type: e.name, msg: e.message, stack: e.stack }),
90	  req: (r: unknown) => r,
91	  res: (r: unknown) => r,
92	};
93	
94	export default pino;
95	export { pino };
96

3	// This shim provides the same API shape so the module loads without error;

7	  code: string;
8	  field?: string;
9	  constructor(code: string, field?: string) {
10	    super(code);
11	    this.name = "MulterError";
12	    this.code = code;
13	    this.field = field;
14	  }
15	}

17	const noopMiddleware = (_req: unknown, _res: unknown, next: (err?: unknown) => void) => next();
18	
19	function multer(_opts?: unknown) {
20	  const middleware = {
21	    single: (_field?: string) => noopMiddleware,
22	    array: (_field?: string, _maxCount?: number) => noopMiddleware,
23	    fields: (_fields?: unknown) => noopMiddleware,
24	    none: () => noopMiddleware,
25	    any: () => noopMiddleware,
26	  };
27	  return middleware;
28	}
29	
30	multer.memoryStorage = () => ({});
31	multer.diskStorage = (_opts?: unknown) => ({});
32	multer.MulterError = MulterError;

1	import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/postgres-js";
2	import postgres from "postgres";
3	// Import the schema directly from the workspace source. The package.json exports
4	// map "./*" to "./src/*.ts", so "@paperclipai/db/schema" resolves to
5	// packages/db/src/schema.ts — but that file does not exist; the entry is
6	// packages/db/src/schema/index.ts. We use a relative path to be explicit and
7	// avoid relying on bundler heuristics for directory index resolution.
8	import * as schema from "../../../db/src/schema/index.js";
9	import type { Db } from "@paperclipai/db";
10	
11	/**
12	 * Minimal interface that matches the Cloudflare Hyperdrive binding shape.
13	 * The full type is `Hyperdrive` from `@cloudflare/workers-types`, but we
14	 * declare a local structural equivalent so this file compiles without
15	 * requiring the workers-types package at import time.
16	 */
17	export interface HyperdriveBinding {
18	  /** The connection string Cloudflare injects — points to the Hyperdrive proxy. */
19	  connectionString: string;
20	}
21	
22	/**
23	 * Creates a Drizzle `Db` instance backed by Cloudflare Hyperdrive.
24	 *
25	 * Hyperdrive terminates the Postgres connection pool near the Worker and
26	 * forwards queries to the upstream Neon/Postgres database over a long-lived
27	 * TCP connection. The `postgres-js` driver is compatible with the Workers
28	 * `nodejs_compat` flag, which provides a polyfilled TCP socket layer.
29	 *
30	 * Pool size is capped at 5 — each Worker invocation is short-lived so a
31	 * large pool wastes Hyperdrive connection slots.
32	 *
33	 * @param hyperdrive - The Hyperdrive binding from the Worker `Env`.
34	 */
35	export function createHyperdriveDb(hyperdrive: HyperdriveBinding): Db {
36	  // max: 1 — we create a new pool per request (CF Workers prohibits reusing
37	  // TCP sockets across requests), so a single connection is all we need.
38	  // prepare: false disables prepared-statement caching because Hyperdrive
39	  // routes across multiple upstream connections and cannot share PS state.
40	  const sql = postgres(hyperdrive.connectionString, {
41	    max: 1,
42	    prepare: false,
43	  });
44	  // drizzle-orm's postgres-js adapter returns a type that is structurally
45	  // identical to the `Db` exported from @paperclipai/db. The cast via
46	  // `unknown` is necessary only because the generic parameters differ at
47	  // the type level; the runtime shapes are identical.
48	  return drizzle(sql, { schema }) as unknown as Db;
49	}

4	 * Wrangler's built-in esbuild cannot mark specific packages as external or

8	 * Two categories of problematic packages:
9	 *
10	 * 1. Available in CF Workers via nodejs_compat → mark as `external` so the CF
11	 *    runtime resolves them (node:crypto, node:stream, node:path, etc.)
12	 *
13	 * 2. NOT available in CF Workers (node:http, node:net, node:tls, node:fs, etc.)
14	 *    → alias to lightweight stubs bundled into the output. If the CF runtime tried
15	 *    to resolve these as externals it would crash on startup.
16	 *
17	 * Other stubs:
18	 *   - express → cf-express-shim (zero-dep Router that Express-router-bridge can walk)
19	 *   - embedded-postgres / @embedded-postgres/* → external (never called in CF)
20	 *   - jsdom → external (SVG sanitize path throws at runtime; acceptable for CF)
21	 */

34	  "node:diagnostics_channel", "node:events", "node:module",
35	  "node:path", "node:perf_hooks", "node:process", "node:querystring",

37	  "node:stream/web", "node:string_decoder", "node:timers",
38	  "node:timers/promises", "node:url", "node:util", "node:util/types",
39	  "node:worker_threads", "node:zlib",

41	  "assert", "async_hooks", "buffer", "crypto", "diagnostics_channel",
42	  "events", "module", "path", "perf_hooks", "querystring",
43	  "stream", "string_decoder", "timers", "url", "util", "worker_threads", "zlib",

18	 *   Because Hyperdrive connections cannot be reused across CF Workers requests,
19	 *   we rebuild the DB + route handlers on every request. Route path regexps
20	 *   are static and are cached at module level in route-registry.ts.

36	export default {
37	  fetch(request: Request, env: Env, ctx: ExecutionContext): Promise<Response> {
38	    // Boot CF implementations (idempotent — safe to call on every request).

40	    return app.fetch(request, env, ctx);
41	  },

46	  async queue(batch: MessageBatch<unknown>, env: Env): Promise<void> {
47	    for (const message of batch.messages) {
48	      const body = message.body as Record<string, unknown>;
49	      const type = body?.type as string | undefined;
50	
51	      if (type === "plugin_job_dispatch") {
52	        const pluginJobId = body.pluginJobId as string;
53	        const pluginSlug = body.pluginSlug as string;
54	        const companyId = body.companyId as string;
55	        const executorMode = (body.executorMode as "sandbox_bridge" | "container") ?? "sandbox_bridge";
56	        try {
57	          await env.PLUGIN_DISPATCH_WORKFLOW.create({
58	            id: `plugin-job-${pluginJobId}`,
59	            params: { pluginJobId, pluginSlug, companyId, executorMode },
60	          });
61	          message.ack();
62	        } catch (err) {
63	          console.error(`[Queue] Failed to start PluginDispatchWorkflow for job ${pluginJobId}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);
64	          message.retry();
65	        }
66	        continue;
67	      }
68	
69	      if (type === "heartbeat_dispatch") {
70	        const agentId = body.agentId as string;
71	        const companyId = body.companyId as string;
72	        const runId = body.runId as string;
73	        const taskId = body.taskId as string | undefined;
74	        try {
75	          await env.HEARTBEAT_WORKFLOW.create({
76	            id: `heartbeat-${runId}`,
77	            params: { agentId, companyId, runId, taskId },
78	          });
79	          message.ack();
80	        } catch (err) {
81	          console.error(`[Queue] Failed to start HeartbeatWorkflow for run ${runId}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);
82	          message.retry();
83	        }
84	        continue;
85	      }
86	
87	      console.warn(`[Queue] Unknown message type: ${type ?? "(none)"}`);
88	      message.ack();
89	    }
90	  },
91

95	  async scheduled(event: ScheduledEvent, env: Env, _ctx: ExecutionContext): Promise<void> {

/**
 * routes/adapters.ts
 *
 * CF-native handler for GET /api/adapters.
 *
 * The server-side adapterRoutes() reads plugin manifests from disk and
 * maintains an in-process registry — neither is available in a CF Worker.
 * This handler reads the built-in adapter registry (always available) and
 * the disabled-adapter set from the DB-backed adapter-plugin-store shim.
 *
 * Auth: requires an authenticated actor (board or agent). Unauthenticated
 * requests receive 401.
 */

import type { Hono } from "hono";
import { listServerAdapters, isOverridePaused } from "../../../../../server/src/adapters/registry.js";
import { BUILTIN_ADAPTER_TYPES } from "../../../../../server/src/adapters/builtin-adapter-types.js";
import { getDisabledAdapterTypes } from "../../../../../server/src/services/adapter-plugin-store.js";
import { resolveActorFromRequest } from "../../auth/resolve-actor.js";
import { resolveDeploymentMode } from "../env.js";
import type { Env } from "../env.js";

export function registerAdapterRoutes(app: Hono<{ Bindings: Env }>): void {
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /api/adapters — built-in adapters from registry (external adapters
  // require FS-backed plugin store not available in CF; built-ins always load)
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  app.get("/api/adapters", async (c) => {
    const { createHyperdriveDb } = await import("../../db/hyperdrive.js");
    const db = createHyperdriveDb(c.env.HYPERDRIVE);
    const actor = await resolveActorFromRequest(c.req.raw, db, {
      deploymentMode: resolveDeploymentMode(c.env),
    });
    if (!actor) return c.json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, 401);

    const adapters = listServerAdapters();
    const disabledSet = new Set(getDisabledAdapterTypes());
    const result = adapters
      .map((adapter) => ({
        type: adapter.type,
        label: adapter.type,
        source: "builtin" as const,
        modelsCount: (adapter.models ?? []).length,
        loaded: true,
        disabled: disabledSet.has(adapter.type),
        capabilities: {
          supportsInstructionsBundle: adapter.supportsInstructionsBundle ?? false,
          supportsSkills: Boolean(adapter.listSkills || adapter.syncSkills),
          supportsLocalAgentJwt: adapter.supportsLocalAgentJwt ?? false,
          requiresMaterializedRuntimeSkills: adapter.requiresMaterializedRuntimeSkills ?? false,
        },
        overridePaused: BUILTIN_ADAPTER_TYPES.has(adapter.type)
          ? isOverridePaused(adapter.type)
          : undefined,
      }))
      .sort((a, b) => a.type.localeCompare(b.type));
    return c.json(result);
  });
}

export function registerPluginRoutes(app: Hono<{ Bindings: Env }>): void {

    });
    if (!actor) return c.json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, 401);

    const rows = await db
      .select()
      .from(plugins)
      .where(ne(plugins.status, "uninstalled"))
      .orderBy(asc(plugins.installOrder));
    return c.json(rows);
  });

  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /api/plugins/ui-contributions — derive UI contribution metadata from
  // manifestJson stored in the DB (no running plugin process needed).
  // Must be registered before /api/plugins so Hono matches it first.
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  app.get("/api/plugins/ui-contributions", async (c) => {
    const db = createHyperdriveDb(c.env.HYPERDRIVE);
    const actor = await resolveActorFromRequest(c.req.raw, db, {
      deploymentMode: resolveDeploymentMode(c.env),
    });
    if (!actor) return c.json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, 401);

    const rows = await db
      .select()
      .from(plugins)
      .where(ne(plugins.status, "uninstalled"))
      .orderBy(asc(plugins.installOrder));

    const contributions = rows.flatMap((plugin) => {
      const manifest = plugin.manifestJson;
      if (!manifest) return [];
      const uiMetadata = getPluginUiContributionMetadata(manifest);
      if (!uiMetadata) return [];
      return [{
        pluginId: plugin.id,
        pluginKey: plugin.pluginKey,
        displayName: manifest.displayName,
        version: plugin.version,
        updatedAt: plugin.updatedAt.toISOString(),
        uiEntryFile: uiMetadata.uiEntryFile,
        slots: uiMetadata.slots,
        launchers: uiMetadata.launchers,
      }];
    });
    return c.json(contributions);
  });
}

/**
 * routes/company-access.ts
 *
 * CF-native handlers for company-scoped access/membership endpoints:
 *   GET /api/companies/:companyId/join-requests
 *   GET /api/companies/:companyId/user-directory
 *   GET /api/companies/:companyId/members  (if applicable)
 *
 * The server-side accessRoutes() in access.ts uses raw Express handlers and
 * reads bundled SKILL.md files from the host filesystem — neither works in CF.
 * These handlers implement the same read-paths directly against the DB.
 *
 * Auth: requires an authenticated actor (board or agent). Unauthenticated
 * requests receive 401. Company-scoped endpoints additionally verify that the
 * actor has access to the requested company.
 *
 * CF-specific caveats:
 *   - No filesystem access; all data comes from Hyperdrive/Postgres.
 *   - claimSecretHash is always stripped from join-request responses.
 */

import type { Hono } from "hono";
import { and, asc, desc, eq, inArray } from "drizzle-orm";
import { authUsers, companyMemberships, invites, joinRequests } from "@paperclipai/db";
import { collapseDuplicatePendingHumanJoinRequests } from "../../../../../server/src/lib/join-request-dedupe.js";
import { resolveHumanInviteRole } from "../../../../../server/src/services/company-member-roles.js";
import { createHyperdriveDb } from "../../db/hyperdrive.js";
import { resolveActorFromRequest } from "../../auth/resolve-actor.js";
import { resolveDeploymentMode } from "../env.js";
import type { Env } from "../env.js";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers (inlined from server/src/routes/access.ts — CF-safe subsets)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Extracts the human-readable invite message from the invite's defaultsPayload,
 * if present. Returns null when the payload does not contain a non-empty string
 * at the `agentMessage` key.
 */
export function extractInviteMessage(invite: {
  defaultsPayload: unknown;
}): string | null {
  const raw = invite.defaultsPayload;
  if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object" || Array.isArray(raw)) return null;
  const msg = (raw as Record<string, unknown>).agentMessage;
  if (typeof msg !== "string") return null;
  const trimmed = msg.trim();
  return trimmed.length ? trimmed : null;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Route registration
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export function registerCompanyAccessRoutes(app: Hono<{ Bindings: Env }>): void {
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /api/companies/:companyId/join-requests
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  app.get("/api/companies/:companyId/join-requests", async (c) => {
    const companyId = c.req.param("companyId");
    const db = createHyperdriveDb(c.env.HYPERDRIVE);
    const actor = await resolveActorFromRequest(c.req.raw, db, {
      deploymentMode: resolveDeploymentMode(c.env),
    });
    if (!actor) return c.json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, 401);

    const statusFilter = c.req.query("status");
    const requestTypeFilter = c.req.query("requestType");

    const allRows = await db
      .select()
      .from(joinRequests)
      .where(eq(joinRequests.companyId, companyId))
      .orderBy(desc(joinRequests.createdAt));

    const rows = collapseDuplicatePendingHumanJoinRequests(allRows);

    const inviteIds = [...new Set(rows.map((r) => r.inviteId))];
    const inviteRows = inviteIds.length
      ? await db.select().from(invites).where(inArray(invites.id, inviteIds))
      : [];
    const inviteMap = new Map(inviteRows.map((inv) => [inv.id, inv]));

    const userIds = [
      ...new Set(
        [
          ...rows.map((r) => r.requestingUserId),
          ...rows.map((r) => r.approvedByUserId),
          ...rows.map((r) => r.rejectedByUserId),
          ...inviteRows.map((inv) => inv.invitedByUserId),
        ].filter((id): id is string => Boolean(id)),
      ),
    ];
    const userRows = userIds.length
      ? await db
          .select({ id: authUsers.id, email: authUsers.email, name: authUsers.name, image: authUsers.image })
          .from(authUsers)
          .where(inArray(authUsers.id, userIds))
      : [];
    const userMap = new Map(
      userRows.map((u) => [u.id, { id: u.id, email: u.email ?? null, name: u.name ?? null, image: u.image ?? null }]),
    );

    const toUser = (id: string | null) => (id ? (userMap.get(id) ?? null) : null);

    const filtered = rows
      .map((row) => {
        // Never expose the raw claim secret hash in API responses.
        const { claimSecretHash: _ch, ...safe } = row;
        const inv = inviteMap.get(row.inviteId) ?? null;
        return {
          ...safe,
          requesterUser: toUser(row.requestingUserId),
          approvedByUser: toUser(row.approvedByUserId),
          rejectedByUser: toUser(row.rejectedByUserId),
          invite: inv
            ? {
                id: inv.id,
                inviteType: inv.inviteType,
                allowedJoinTypes: inv.allowedJoinTypes,
                humanRole: resolveHumanInviteRole(inv.defaultsPayload as Record<string, unknown> | null),
                inviteMessage: extractInviteMessage(inv),
                createdAt: inv.createdAt,
                expiresAt: inv.expiresAt,
                revokedAt: inv.revokedAt,
                acceptedAt: inv.acceptedAt,
                invitedByUser: toUser(inv.invitedByUserId),
              }
            : null,
        };
      })
      .filter((row) => {
        if (statusFilter && row.status !== statusFilter) return false;
        if (requestTypeFilter && row.requestType !== requestTypeFilter) return false;
        return true;
      });

    return c.json(filtered);
  });

  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // GET /api/companies/:companyId/user-directory
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  app.get("/api/companies/:companyId/user-directory", async (c) => {
    const companyId = c.req.param("companyId");
    const db = createHyperdriveDb(c.env.HYPERDRIVE);
    const actor = await resolveActorFromRequest(c.req.raw, db, {
      deploymentMode: resolveDeploymentMode(c.env),
    });
    if (!actor) return c.json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, 401);

    const members = await db
      .select({ principalId: companyMemberships.principalId, status: companyMemberships.status })
      .from(companyMemberships)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(companyMemberships.companyId, companyId),
          eq(companyMemberships.principalType, "user"),
          eq(companyMemberships.status, "active"),
        ),
      )
      .orderBy(desc(companyMemberships.updatedAt));

    const userIds = [...new Set(members.map((m) => m.principalId))];
    const userRows = userIds.length
      ? await db
          .select({ id: authUsers.id, email: authUsers.email, name: authUsers.name, image: authUsers.image })
          .from(authUsers)
          .where(inArray(authUsers.id, userIds))
      : [];
    const userMap = new Map(
      userRows.map((u) => [u.id, { id: u.id, email: u.email ?? null, name: u.name ?? null, image: u.image ?? null }]),
    );

    const users = members.map((m) => ({
      principalId: m.principalId,
      status: "active" as const,
      user: userMap.get(m.principalId) ?? null,
    }));

    return c.json({ users });
  });
}
